sentences.zh: 孔愉

translations.literal: Kong Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Kong Yu.

translations.literal: The heading opens with the bracket 〈.
translations.idiomatic: An opening corner bracket introduces the subsection listing collateral kin treated below.

sentences.zh: （子汪 安國 弟祗 從子坦嚴 從弟群 群子沉）〉

translations.literal: (Listed hereafter: his sons Wang and Anguo; younger brother Zhi; nephews Tan and Yan; younger cousin Qun; Qun's son Shen.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The chapter also treats Kong Yu's sons Wang and Anguo, his brother Zhi, his nephews Tan and Yan, his cousin Qun, and Qun's son Shen.〉

sentences.zh: 丁潭 張茂 陶回

translations.literal: Ding Tan; Zhang Mao; Tao Hui.
translations.idiomatic: This volume continues with Ding Tan, Zhang Mao, and Tao Hui.

sentences.zh: 孔愉，字敬康，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Yu, courtesy name Jingkang, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yu, whose courtesy name was Jingkang, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先世居梁國。

translations.literal: His ancestors for generations dwelt in Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had lived for generations in Liang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖潛，太子少傅，漢末避地會稽，因家焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qian was Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; at the end of the Han he fled to Kuaiji and there settled.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qian had served as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; when the Han dynasty collapsed he took refuge in Kuaiji and made it his home.

sentences.zh: 祖竺，吳豫章太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhu was governor of Yuzhang under Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhu had been governor of Yuzhang for Eastern Wu.

sentences.zh: 父恬，湘東太守。

translations.literal: His father Tian was governor of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kong Tian had served as governor of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 從兄侃，大司農。

translations.literal: Elder cousin Kan was Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: His senior cousin Kong Kan had reached the post of Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 俱有名江左。

translations.literal: All had reputation east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: All of them were celebrated in the region south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 愉年十三而孤，養祖母以孝聞，與同郡張茂字偉康、丁潭字世康齊名，時人號曰「會稽三康」。

translations.literal: Yu at thirteen was orphaned; he supported his grandmother and was heard of for filial piety. With Zhang Mao of the same commandery, courtesy name Weikang, and Ding Tan, courtesy name Shikang, he shared equal fame, and people of the time called them "the Three Kang of Kuaiji."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yu lost his father at thirteen; he cared for his grandmother and earned a reputation for filial devotion. Alongside Zhang Mao of the same commandery (courtesy Weikang) and Ding Tan (courtesy Shikang), he was equally renowned, and contemporaries dubbed them the "Three Kang of Kuaiji."

sentences.zh: 吳平，愉遷於洛。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, Yu moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell, Kong Yu relocated to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 惠帝末，歸鄉里，行至江淮間，遇石冰、封雲為亂，雲逼愉為參軍，不從將殺之，賴雲司馬張統營救獲免。

translations.literal: Toward the end of Emperor Hui he returned toward his home; traveling between the Jiang and Huai he encountered the rebellion of Shi Bing and Feng Yun. Yun compelled Yu to serve as staff officer; when Yu did not comply Yun was about to kill him, but thanks to the rescue efforts of Yun's aide Zhang Tong he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Hui's reign he headed home; between the Yangzi and the Huai he ran into the uprising led by Shi Bing and Feng Yun. Feng Yun tried to force Kong Yu onto his staff as an adviser; when Yu refused, Yun prepared to execute him, but Zhang Tong, Yun's aide-de-camp, intervened and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 東還會稽，人新安山中，改姓孫氏，以稼穡讀書為務，信著鄉里。

translations.literal: He went east back to Kuaiji and entered the mountains of Xin'an, changed his surname to Sun, took farming and reading as his occupation, and trustworthiness was noted in the village.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled east to Kuaiji and withdrew into the Xin'an hills, adopting the surname Sun and devoting himself to farming and study until his integrity was widely trusted in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 後忽舍去，皆謂為神人，而為之立祠。

translations.literal: Later he suddenly left; all said he was a divine man and built a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he suddenly vanished, locals took him for an immortal and erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，元帝始以安東將軍鎮揚土，命愉為參軍。

translations.literal: During Yongjia, the Prince of Langye first took post as General Who Guards the East and governed Yangzhou territory, and ordered Yu as army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongjia era the Prince of Langye—later Yuan Emperor—first held Yangzhou as General Who Guards the East and appointed Kong Yu as his military adviser.

sentences.zh: 邦族尋求，莫知所在。

translations.literal: Clansmen sought him; none knew where he was.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsmen searched for him, but no one could find him.

sentences.zh: 建興初，始出應召。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianxing he at last emerged and answered the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the opening of the Jianxing era did he emerge and answer the court's call.

sentences.zh: 為丞相掾，仍除駙馬都尉、參丞相軍事，時年已五十矣。

translations.literal: He served as aide to the Chancellor of State and was then appointed Chief Commandant of Attendant Cavalry and joined the Chancellor's military staff; at the time he was already fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He became an aide to the Chancellor of State, then Chief Commandant of Attendant Cavalry and a member of the Chancellor's military staff—by then he was fifty years old.

sentences.zh: 以討華軼功，封余不亭侯。

translations.literal: For merit in the campaign against Hua Yi he was enfeoffed as marquis of Yubu ting.
translations.idiomatic: He earned the title Marquis of Yubu township for his part in defeating Hua Yi.

sentences.zh: 愉嘗行經餘不亭，見籠龜于路者，愉買而放之溪中，龜中流左顧者數四。

translations.literal: Yu once traveled past Yubu ting and saw someone on the road with a tortoise in a cage; Yu bought it and released it into the stream, and the tortoise in midstream looked left several times.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Yubu township once, Kong Yu bought a caged tortoise from a roadside vendor and released it into the creek; midstream the animal turned its head left—again and again.

sentences.zh: 及是，鑄侯印，而印龜左顧，三鑄如初。

translations.literal: When it came time to cast the marquis's seal, the tortoise on the seal faced left; they cast it three times and each time as at first.
translations.idiomatic: When his seal was cast, the tortoise motif faced left all three times—just as the living tortoise had behaved.

sentences.zh: 印工以告，愉乃悟，遂佩焉。

translations.literal: The seal-maker reported it; Yu then understood and thereafter wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The engraver reported the oddity; Kong Yu grasped the omen and gladly wore the seal.

sentences.zh: 帝為晉王，使長兼中書郎。

translations.literal: When the Emperor became Prince of Jin, he assigned Yu provisionally as Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the sovereign became Prince of Jin, Kong Yu served provisionally as a gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 于時刁協、劉隗用事，王導頗見疏遠。

translations.literal: At that time Diao Xie and Liu Wei wielded power, and Wang Dao was rather sidelined.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie and Liu Wei dominated court affairs then, while Wang Dao found himself increasingly marginalized.

sentences.zh: 愉陳導忠賢，有佐命之勳，謂事無大小皆宜諮訪。

translations.literal: Yu declared Dao loyal and worthy, with merit in aiding the founding mandate, and said matters great and small should all be consulted with him.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yu argued that Wang Dao was loyal and capable, had helped establish the dynasty, and ought to be consulted on every decision, large or small.

sentences.zh: 由是不合旨，出為司徒左長史，累遷吳興太守。

translations.literal: Thereby he did not accord with the intent; he was sent out as senior clerk to the left of the Minister of Education and promoted in stages to governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: That advice displeased the throne, so he was posted out as senior clerk of the Minister of Education's left section and eventually rose to governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 沈充反，愉棄官還京師，拜御史中丞，遷侍中、太常。

translations.literal: When Shen Chong rebelled, Yu resigned his post and returned to the capital; he was appointed Censor-in-chief and promoted to palace attendant and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Chong rose in revolt, Kong Yu quit his post for the capital, received appointment as Censor-in-chief, and advanced to palace attendant and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 及蘇峻反，愉朝服守宗廟。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, Yu in court robes guarded the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun's rebellion he stood guard over the imperial ancestral shrine in full court dress.

sentences.zh: 初，愉為司徒長史，以平南將軍溫嶠母亡遭亂不葬，乃不過其品。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yu was senior clerk to the Minister of Education, because the mother of General Who Pacifies the South Wen Qiao had died amid turmoil and was not buried, he therefore did not pass his evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving as the Minister of Education's senior clerk, Kong Yu had withheld a favorable personnel rating from Wen Qiao—General Who Pacifies the South—because Qiao's mother had died in the chaos and still lay unburied.

sentences.zh: 至是，峻平，而嶠有重功，愉往石頭詣嶠，嶠執愉手而流涕曰：「天下喪亂，忠孝道廢。

translations.literal: When Su Jun was crushed, Qiao had heavy merit; Yu went to Stone Fort to visit Qiao; Qiao grasped Yu's hand and wept, saying, "The realm is ruined and turmoil reigns; loyalty and filial duty are cast aside."
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun fell, Wen Qiao—who had rendered outstanding service—received Kong Yu at Stone Fort. Qiao clasped his hand with tears: "The empire lies in ruins; fidelity and filial piety have been abandoned."

sentences.zh: 能持古人之節，歲寒不凋者，唯君一人耳。

translations.literal: "Those who can uphold the integrity of the ancients and not wither in the year's cold—you alone."
translations.idiomatic: "Among all who could uphold the old standard and stand firm through the bitter winter, you alone remain."

sentences.zh: 」時人咸稱嶠居公而重愉之守正。

translations.literal: People of the time all praised Qiao for occupying high office while respecting Yu's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries applauded Wen Qiao for magnanimity in power and Kong Yu for unbending principle.

sentences.zh: 尋徙大尚書，遷安南將軍、江州刺史，不行。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to senior minister of the masters of writing and promoted to General Who Guards the South and governor of Jiangzhou; he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon shifted to senior minister of the masters of writing and offered General Who Guards the South and governor of Jiangzhou, but declined to assume the latter posts.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書右僕射，領東海王師。

translations.literal: He was shifted to vice director of the right of the masters of writing and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to vice director of the right of the masters of writing while tutoring the Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左僕射。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted to vice director of the left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became vice director of the left.

sentences.zh: 咸和八年，詔曰：「尚書令玩、左僕射愉並恪居官次，祿不代耕。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianhe, an edict said: "Director of State Affairs Wan and Vice Director Yu both steadfastly remain at their posts; their salaries do not replace farming."
translations.idiomatic: In Xianhe 8 an edict declared: "Director Wan and Vice Director Kong Yu steadfastly fill their offices though their stipends scarcely feed a household."

sentences.zh: 端右任重，先朝所崇，其給玩親信三十人，愉二十人，稟賜。

translations.literal: "The burden at the head of the administration is weighty and was esteemed by former courts; grant Wan thirty trusted attendants and Yu twenty, with stipends."
translations.idiomatic: "Their seats at the helm are heavy trusts once honored by earlier courts—award Wan thirty personal attendants and Kong Yu twenty, with grain allowances."

sentences.zh: 」愉上疏固讓，優詔不許。

translations.literal: " Yu submitted a memorial firmly declining; a gracious edict refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yu memorialized to decline the gift; a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 重表曰：「臣以朽暗，忝廁朝右，而以惰劣，無益毗佐。

translations.literal: He submitted another memorial: "Your servant, rotten and dim, has been admitted among the court's right ranks, yet through laziness and inferiority has benefited nothing in assisting governance."
translations.idiomatic: Another memorial followed: "I am a dull, undeserving man perched among the senior ministers; sloth has kept me from aiding governance in any real way."

sentences.zh: 方今強寇未殄，疆場日駭，政煩役重，百姓困苦，奸吏擅威，暴人肆虐。

translations.literal: Now the mighty foe is not yet destroyed; the borders are daily alarmed; government is tangled and service heavy; the common people suffer hardship; wicked clerks abuse authority; violent men run rampant.
translations.idiomatic: The great enemy remains undefeated; the frontiers flare daily; administration is tangled and corvée burdens crush the people; cruel officials wield unchecked power and predators ravage the land.

sentences.zh: 大弊之後，倉庫空虛，功勞之士，賞報不足，困悴之餘，未見拯恤，呼嗟之怨，人鬼感動。

translations.literal: After great harm the granaries stand empty; men of merit lack adequate reward; those worn down have seen no relief; the cries of lament move both men and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: After such devastation the treasuries are bare; heroes go underpaid; the exhausted receive no relief; lamentations stir living and dead alike.

sentences.zh: 宜並官省職，貶食節用，勤撫其人，以濟其艱。

translations.literal: Offices should be merged and duties cut; salaries reduced and expenses restrained; the people diligently comforted to relieve their hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Merge offices, trim posts, cut salaries and spending, and diligently succor the people through this calamity.

sentences.zh: 臣等不能讚揚大化，糾明刑政，而偷安高位，橫受寵給，無德而祿，殃必及之，不敢橫受殊施，以重罪戾。

translations.literal: Your servants cannot extend your transforming influence or rectify punishments and administration, yet we steal ease in high place and freely receive lavish grants—virtue without matching emolument brings calamity; we dare not rashly accept extraordinary favor and thereby deepen our guilt.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot magnify your transforming influence nor clarify law and policy, yet we idle in lofty posts and soak up privilege—salary without merit invites disaster—so we dare not accept such extraordinary largesse and deepen our guilt.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: His plea was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial court accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 王導聞而非之，於都坐謂愉曰：「君言奸吏擅威，暴人肆虐，為患是誰？

translations.literal: Wang Dao heard this and disapproved; at the joint session in the capital he said to Yu, "When you speak of wicked clerks abusing authority and violent men running rampant, who is the trouble?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao took offense. At the metropolitan assembly he challenged Kong Yu: "You blame corrupt clerks and cruel bullies—whom exactly do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 」愉欲大論朝廷得失，陸玩抑之乃止。

translations.literal: Yu wished to debate at length the court's gains and losses; Lu Wan restrained him and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yu was ready to dissect the court's failings in detail, but Lu Wan checked him and he fell silent.

sentences.zh: 後導將以趙胤為護軍，愉謂導曰：「中興以來，處此官者，周伯仁、應思遠耳。

translations.literal: Later Dao was about to appoint Zhao Yin as Defender-in-Chief; Yu said to Dao, "Since the restoration, those who have held this office have been Zhou Bozhou and Ying Siyuan alone."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dao planned to make Zhao Yin Defender-in-Chief, Kong Yu objected: "Since the restoration only Zhou Bozhou and Ying Siyuan have held that post."

sentences.zh: 今誠乏才，豈宜以趙胤居之邪！

translations.literal: "If talent is truly lacking, should Zhao Yin occupy it?"
translations.idiomatic: "Even if qualified men are scarce, can Zhao Yin rightly fill it?"

sentences.zh: 」導不從。

translations.literal: Dao did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 其守正如此。

translations.literal: His integrity was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 由是為導所銜。

translations.literal: Thereby he was resented by Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao hence harbored a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 後省左右僕射，以愉為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Later the left and right vice directors were abolished; Yu was made vice director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the paired vice directorships were merged, Kong Yu became sole vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 愉年在懸車，累乞骸骨，不許，轉護軍將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Yu had reached the age to hang up the carriage-curtains; he repeatedly begged to surrender his bones but was refused; he was transferred to Defender-in-Chief and given additional title as regular attendant at court.
translations.idiomatic: Past the age when officials retire, Kong Yu repeatedly asked leave to resign; the throne refused and instead named him Defender-in-Chief with concurrent appointment as regular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 復徙領軍將軍，加金紫光祿大夫，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was moved again to General Who Guards the Army, added title as Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and concurrently overseer of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He then shifted to General Who Guards the Army, received the honorary rank of grand master of golden seal and purple ribbon, and headed the National University.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出為鎮軍將軍、會稽內史，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as General Who Guards the Army and interior governor of Kuaiji, with additional title as palace attendant regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left the capital as General Who Guards the Army and interior governor of Kuaiji, with additional status as palace attendant regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 句章縣有漢時舊陂，毀廢數百年。

translations.literal: In Gouzhang county there was an old dyke from Han times; it had lain ruined for several hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Gouzhang county still held a Han-era irrigation works ruined for centuries.

sentences.zh: 愉自巡行，修復故堰，溉田二百餘頃，皆成良業。

translations.literal: Yu personally toured the area, repaired the former weir, and irrigated over two hundred qing of fields; all became good farmland.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yu inspected it himself, rebuilt the old dam, and brought more than two hundred qing under irrigation—all prime farmland again.

sentences.zh: 在郡三年，乃營山陰湖南侯山下數畝地為宅，草屋數間，便棄官居之。

translations.literal: After three years in the commandery he acquired several mu of land below Mount Hou south of Shanyin Lake as a residence, a few thatched huts, then resigned office and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Three years into his tenure he laid out a few mu beneath Mount Hou south of Shanyin Lake, threw up a cluster of thatched cottages, resigned his post, and lived there.

sentences.zh: 送資數百萬，悉無所取。

translations.literal: Funds offered him amounted to several million cash; he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Locals pressed millions in cash on him; he refused every coin.

sentences.zh: 病篤，遺令斂以時服，鄉邑義賵，一不得受。

translations.literal: When gravely ill he left instructions to be buried in timely dress and that condolence gifts from the village—none might be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Stricken mortally, he ordered burial in ordinary clothes and forbade any condolence offerings from the district.

sentences.zh: 年七十五，咸康八年卒。

translations.literal: At age seventy-five he died in the eighth year of Xiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five in Xiankang 8.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry, offices equal to the Three Dukes, with posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General of Chariots and Cavalry with privilege to maintain an independent command matching the Three Dukes, and canonized as "Steadfast" (Zhen).

sentences.zh: 三子：訚、汪、安國。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Yin, Wang, and Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: He left three sons—Yin, Wang, and Anguo.

sentences.zh: 訚嗣爵，位至建安太守。

translations.literal: Yin inherited the title and rose to governor of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yin succeeded to the marquisate and rose to governor of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 訚子靜，字季恭，再為會稽內史，累遷尚書左僕射，加後將軍。

translations.literal: Yin's son Jing, courtesy name Jigong, twice served as interior governor of Kuaiji and was promoted in stages to vice director of the left of the masters of writing with additional title as General of the Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son Kong Jing (courtesy Jigong) twice governed Kuaiji as interior governor and eventually reached vice director of the left of the masters of writing with the additional title General of the Rear Guard.

sentences.zh: 汪字德澤，好學有志行，孝武帝時位至侍中。

translations.literal: Wang, courtesy name Deze, loved learning and had principled conduct; under Emperor Xiaowu he reached palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wang, courtesy Deze, loved scholarship and conducted himself with principle; under Emperor Xiaowu he rose to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時茹千秋以佞媚見幸于會稽王道子，汪屢言之於帝，帝不納。

translations.literal: At that time Ru Qianqiu through flattery won favor with the Prince of Kuaiji Wang Daozi; Wang repeatedly spoke of this to the emperor; the emperor did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Qianqiu curried favor with Prince Daozi of Kuaiji; Kong Wang repeatedly warned the emperor, who brushed him off.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書太常卿，以不合意，求出。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Education and Minister of Ceremonies; because it did not suit his wishes, he sought a post outside.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to the ministries of masters of writing and of ceremonies, he found the roles uncongenial and requested a provincial assignment.

sentences.zh: 為假節、都督交廣二州諸軍事、征虜將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史，甚有政績，為嶺表所稱。

translations.literal: He held credential-bearing authority as commander of all military affairs of Jiao and Guang provinces, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, Colonel Who Pacifies the Yue, and governor of Guangzhou, with very outstanding administrative record and praise south of the ridges.
translations.idiomatic: As credential-bearing governor of Guangzhou and commander over Jiao and Guang—with the titles General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Colonel Who Pacifies the Yue—he governed so well that he won acclaim throughout the Lingnan region.

sentences.zh: 太元十七年卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Taiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year of the Taiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 安國字安國，年小諸兄三十餘歲。

translations.literal: Anguo, courtesy name Anguo, was more than thirty years younger than his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo bore the same courtesy name as his formal name and was more than thirty years junior to his brothers.

sentences.zh: 群從諸兄並乏才名，以富強自立，唯安國與汪少厲孤貧之操。

translations.literal: The gathered elder cousins and brothers all lacked talent and reputation and relied on wealth and strength to establish themselves; only Anguo and Wang in youth cultivated integrity amid orphan poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Among his cousins and elder brothers none had won literary fame—they leaned on wealth and force—yet Anguo and Wang alone embraced austerity and endured poverty in youth.

sentences.zh: 汪既以直亮稱，安國亦以儒素顯。

translations.literal: Wang was already famed for straightforward brightness; Anguo also displayed through Confucian simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Where Wang was celebrated for blunt integrity, Anguo made his mark as a sober Ru scholar.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝時甚蒙禮遇，仕歷侍中、太常。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu he received great courteous treatment; in office he served as palace attendant and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu treated him with exceptional favor; his career ran through palace attendant and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，安國形素贏瘦，服衰絰，涕泗竟日，見者以為真孝，再為會稽內史、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Anguo's frame was always emaciated and thin; he wore mourning headband and sash and wept all day; those who saw thought him truly filial; he twice served as interior governor of Kuaiji and General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor passed away, Anguo—already gaunt—donned hemp mourning and wept the whole day through; observers deemed his grief utterly sincere. He twice served as Kuaiji's interior governor and as General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 安帝隆安中下詔曰：「領軍將軍孔安國貞慎清正，出內播譽，可以本官領東海王師，必能導達津梁，依仁遊藝。

translations.literal: Under Emperor An, in the Long'an era an edict said: "General Who Leads the Army Kong Anguo is chaste, cautious, upright, and pure; within and without his fame spreads; he may with his present office tutor the Prince of Donghai; assuredly he can guide and open ford and bridge, relying on benevolence and roaming in the arts."
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor An's Long'an era an edict praised Kong Anguo—General Who Leads the Army—for discretion and integrity celebrated inside and outside the court, and authorized him to tutor the Prince of Donghai while keeping his military title, confident he could shepherd the heir across life's crossings through humane cultivation.

sentences.zh: 」後曆尚書左右僕射。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as vice director of the left and right of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He subsequently served as vice director of both the left and right of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 義熙四年卒，贈左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yixi he died; he was posthumously awarded senior grand master of the left.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yixi 4 and was posthumously honored as senior grand master of the left.

sentences.zh: 祗字承祖。

translations.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhi's courtesy name was Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 太守周劄命為功曹史。

translations.literal: Governor Zhou Zha appointed him clerk of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhou Zha named him clerk for the bureau of merit.

sentences.zh: 劄為沈充所害，故人賓吏莫敢近者。

translations.literal: Zha was murdered by Shen Chong; former friends, retainers, and clerks none dared approach.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Chong killed Zhou Zha, former friends and staff kept their distance—none dared go near the body.

sentences.zh: 祗冒刃號哭，親行殯禮，送喪還義興，時人義之。

translations.literal: Zhi braved blades and wailed aloud; he personally carried out funeral rites and escorted the coffin back to Yixing; people of the time deemed him righteous.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhi risked the blades to keen over him, personally conducted the obsequies, and convoyed the coffin home to Yixing—contemporaries hailed his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 坦字君平。

translations.literal: Tan, courtesy name Junping.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan's courtesy name was Junping.

sentences.zh: 祖沖，丹陽太守。

translations.literal: Grandfather Chong was governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kong Chong had governed Danyang.

sentences.zh: 父侃，大司農。

translations.literal: Father Kan was Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kong Kan held the post of Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 坦少方直，有雅望，通《左氏傳》，解屬文。

translations.literal: Tan in youth was square and upright, had elegant reputation, comprehended the Zuo Commentary, and understood composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Kong Tan was upright and commanded respect; he mastered the Zuo Commentary and could compose polished prose.

sentences.zh: 元帝為晉王，以坦為世子文學。

translations.literal: When Yuan Emperor was Prince of Jin, he appointed Tan as literary attendant to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: While still Prince of Jin, Emperor Yuan appointed Kong Tan literary scholar to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 東宮建，補太子舍人，遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: When the eastern palace was established, he was supplemented as gentleman attendant of the heir apparent and promoted to gentleman of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Once the heir's residence stood, Kong Tan became a gentleman attendant of the heir apparent and then a gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 時台郎初到，普加策試，帝手策問曰：「吳興徐馥為賊，殺郡將，郡今應舉孝廉不？

translations.literal: At that time when gentlemen of the masters of writing first arrived, universally they were given examination tests; the emperor personally examined asking: "In Wuxing Xu Fu acted as bandit and killed the commandery commander—should the commandery now nominate filial and incorrupt candidates?"
translations.idiomatic: Newly appointed gentlemen of the masters of writing faced palace examinations; the emperor personally asked Kong Tan: "Xu Fu of Wuxing rose as a rebel and murdered the governor—should that commandery still put forward nominees for filial and incorrupt office?"

sentences.zh: 」坦對曰：「四罪不相及，殛鯀而興禹。

translations.literal: Tan replied: "The four crimes do not reach one another; Gun was slain and Yu rose."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan answered: "The canonical 'four crimes' do not implicate the innocent—Gun was executed, yet Yu succeeded him."

sentences.zh: 徐馥為逆，何妨一郡之賢！

translations.literal: Xu Fu acted contrary—what harm to one commandery's worthies!
translations.idiomatic: If Xu Fu rebelled, that still does not indict every worthy man in the commandery.

sentences.zh: 」又問：「奸臣賊子弑君，汙宮瀦宅，莫大之惡也。

translations.literal: He further asked: "Villainous ministers and rebel sons assassinate the ruler, defile palace and flood residence—no greater evil."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed on: "When traitors murder their sovereign and defile the palace—surely the ultimate crime."

sentences.zh: 鄉舊廢四科之選，今何所依？

translations.literal: Since times past the four-category selection has been abolished—on what do we now rely?
translations.idiomatic: The earlier court suspended the four-way recommendation system—what guideline should we follow now?

sentences.zh: 」坦曰：「季平子逐魯昭公，豈可以廢仲尼也！

translations.literal: Tan said: "Ji Pingzi expelled Duke Zhao of Lu—how could one therefore abolish Zhongni!"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan shot back: "Ji Pingzi drove out Duke Zhao of Lu—would anyone scrap Confucius on that account?"

sentences.zh: 」竟不能屈

translations.literal: In the end they could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Try as they might, they could not stump him.

sentences.zh: 先是，以兵亂之後，務存慰悅，遠方秀孝到，不策試，普皆除署。

translations.literal: Earlier, because after military turmoil the aim was to preserve comfort and pleasure, when distant-region cultivated and filial nominees arrived, they were not given examination tests; universally all were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, eager to soothe the realm after war, the court had waived examinations for provincial nominees and handed out posts wholesale.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝申明舊制，皆令試《經》，有不中科，刺史、太守免官。

translations.literal: When it came to this, the emperor clarified the old system; all were ordered to be tested on the classics; if they did not pass the grade, the governor and interior governor were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor reinstated the old rule: every candidate faced classicist examinations, and any failure cost the regional inspector and the governor their posts.

sentences.zh: 太興三年，秀孝多不敢行，其有到者，並托疾。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taixing, cultivated and filial nominees mostly did not dare go; those who arrived all pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Taixing 3 most nominees stayed home; those who did appear pleaded sickness instead of sitting the exam.

sentences.zh: 帝欲除署孝廉，而秀才如前制。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to appoint filial and incorrupt nominees, while for cultivated talents the prior system.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to grant posts to filial-and-incorrupt nominees while leaving the rules for "cultivated talent" candidates unchanged.

sentences.zh: 坦奏議曰：

translations.literal: Tan presented a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan submitted a memorial arguing:

sentences.zh: 臣聞經邦建國，教學為先，移風崇化，莫尚斯矣。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that ordering the realm and founding a state take teaching and learning as foremost; shifting customs and exalting transformation—nothing is nobler than this.
translations.idiomatic: I have always heard that to govern a state one must put schools first—nothing reforms manners or uplifts morals like education.

sentences.zh: 古者且耕且學，三年而通一經，以平康之世，猶假漸漬，積以日月。

translations.literal: In antiquity they farmed and studied; in three years they comprehended one classic; even in an age of peace and health they still relied on gradual soaking, accumulated over days and months.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient scholars farmed while they studied and needed three full years to master a single classic—even in tranquil times mastery came only through long immersion.

sentences.zh: 自喪亂以來，十有餘年，于戈載揚，俎豆禮戢，家廢講誦，國闕庠序，率爾責試，竊以為疑。

translations.literal: Since turmoil began, more than ten years—spears and daggers raised high, sacrificial stands and vessels folded away; households abandoned lectures and recitation, the state lacks schools and academies; rashly to demand examinations—your servant privately finds this doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: For over a decade war has raged, ritual has lapsed, families no longer teach their sons, and the capital has no functioning academy—yet we suddenly insist on examinations; I find that deeply doubtful.

sentences.zh: 然宣下以來，涉曆三載，累遇慶會，遂未一試。

translations.literal: Yet since the proclamation went down, three years have passed, festal assemblies have repeatedly been met, and still not once have they been tested.
translations.idiomatic: Yet three years have passed since the edict, with repeated court festivals, and we still have not held a single examination.

sentences.zh: 揚州諸郡，接近京都，懼累及君父，多不敢行。

translations.literal: In Yangzhou's commanderies, close to the capital, fearing to implicate their lords and fathers, most did not dare go.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou's districts hug the capital: candidates stay away for fear their failure will disgrace their kin.

sentences.zh: 其遠州邊郡，掩誣朝廷，冀於不試，冒昧來赴，既到審試，遂不敢會。

translations.literal: Those in distant provinces and border commanderies deceive the court, hoping to avoid testing; they rashly come; once arrived at review they dare not attend.
translations.idiomatic: Remote jurisdictions lie and claim hardship hoping to dodge the exam; they travel to the capital, yet when the tests loom they feign illness and skip the session.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以不會與不行，其為闕也同。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly considers that not attending and not going—their defect is the same.
translations.idiomatic: In my view skipping the examination and refusing to travel amount to the same failure.

sentences.zh: 若當偏加除署，是為肅法奉憲者失分，僥倖投射者得官，頹風傷教，懼於是始。

translations.literal: If we shall partially grant appointments, this means those who uphold law and honor statutes lose their portion, while those who rely on luck and casting gain office—collapsing manners wound transformation—fear begins here.
translations.idiomatic: If we still appoint men piecemeal, we punish the conscientious and reward the lucky—rotting public ethics begins right there.

sentences.zh: 夫王言如絲，其出如綸，臨事改制，示短天下，人聽有惑，臣竊惜之。

translations.literal: The royal word is like silk; its issuing is like cord; facing affairs altering the system displays shortcoming to the realm; people's hearing has confusion—your servant privately pities this.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial decrees should be as binding as spun silk becoming hawser—changing the rules mid-course exposes weakness and confuses the empire; it saddens me.

sentences.zh: 愚以王命無貳，憲制宜信。

translations.literal: Your servant considers royal commands admit no duplicity; statutory regulations should be trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: The throne must speak once for all; statutes deserve unquestioned faith.

sentences.zh: 去年察舉，一皆策試。

translations.literal: Last year's inspections and recommendations—all were examined by test.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's provincial nominees already faced written examinations.

sentences.zh: 如不能試，可不拘到，遣歸不署。

translations.literal: If they cannot be tested, one may not insist on arrival; send them home without appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When candidates truly cannot sit the exam, waive the requirement to appear—send them home without office rather than fabricating excuses.

sentences.zh: 又秀才雖以事策，亦汜問經義，苟所未學，實難暗通，不足復曲碎垂例，違舊造異。

translations.literal: Moreover although cultivated talents by affair-policy examination also broadly ask classical meanings, if they have not studied it is truly hard to comprehend in darkness; it is not worth again twisting fine precedent, violating the old and creating the strange.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivated-talent candidates answer policy questions yet classics remain fair game—what they never studied they cannot fake; we need not churn petty exceptions that abandon precedent.

sentences.zh: 謂宜因其不會，徐更革制。

translations.literal: Your servant considers it fitting because they do not attend gradually to alter the system.
translations.idiomatic: Because examinees keep absenting themselves, we ought to revise the statute—but gradually.

sentences.zh: 可申明前下，崇修學校，普延五年，以展講習，鈞法齊訓，示人軌則。

translations.literal: May one clarify what was issued before, exalt and repair schools, universally extend five years, so as to unfold lectures and practice, equalize law and align instruction, show people norms.
translations.idiomatic: Reissue the earlier order: rebuild schools, give everyone five full years of instruction, harmonize curricula, and display clear standards for scholars.

sentences.zh: 夫信之與法，為政之綱，施之家室，猶弗可貳，況經國之典而可玩黷乎！

translations.literal: Trust and law are the guideline of governance; applied even to household still cannot be twofold—how much more governing the state's statutes—can they be toyed with?
translations.idiomatic: Faith and statute anchor government; families cannot survive divided loyalty—much less the empire—without inviting contempt for the law.

sentences.zh: 帝納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 聽孝廉申至七年，秀才如故。

translations.literal: Filial and incorrupt nominees were permitted to defer until the seventh year; cultivated talents remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Filial-and-incorrupt candidates might postpone attendance until the seventh year; rules for cultivated talents stayed unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時典客令萬默領諸胡，胡人相誣，朝廷疑默有所偏助，將加大辟。

translations.literal: At that time the Director of Receptions Wan Mo supervised the various Hu; the Hu people accused one another; the court suspected Mo of partial favor and was about to apply capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wan Mo oversaw tribal envoys; mutual accusations among the tribes convinced the court he was playing favorites, and ministers pressed for his execution.

sentences.zh: 坦獨不署，由是被譴，遂棄官歸會稽。

translations.literal: Tan alone did not sign; thereupon he was reprimanded; then he resigned office and returned to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Only Kong Tan withheld his signature; censured for it, he quit office and withdrew to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 久之，除領軍司馬，未赴召。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed marshal of the army-leader's headquarters but did not answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he received appointment as marshal on the army headquarters staff but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 會王敦反，與右衛將軍虞潭俱在會稽起義，而討沈充。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun rebelled, together with General of the Right Guards Yu Tan he both raised troops in Kuaiji and campaigned against Shen Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rose in revolt, Kong Tan joined General Yu Tan of the Right Guards to rally Kuaiji and strike Shen Chong.

sentences.zh: 事平，始就職。

translations.literal: When affairs were pacified, he at last took office.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the rebellion collapsed did he assume his duties.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史王導請為別駕。

translations.literal: Governor of Yangzhou Wang Dao requested him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou governor Wang Dao recruited him as provincial aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，遷尚書左丞，深為台中之所敬憚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianhe he was promoted to assistant director of the left of the masters of writing and was deeply respected and feared within the department.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe he rose to assistant director of the left of the masters of writing and commanded deep respect throughout the boards.

sentences.zh: 尋屬蘇峻反，坦與司徒司馬陶回白王導曰：「及峻未至，宜急斷阜陵之界，守江西當利諸口，彼少我眾，一戰決矣。

translations.literal: Shortly Su Jun rebelled; Tan together with Minister of Education marshal Tao Hui reported to Wang Dao: "Before Jun arrives, one should urgently sever the border at Fuling, guard the various crossings west of the Yangzi at Dangli—they are few, we many—one battle will decide it."
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun rose, Kong Tan and the Minister of Education's marshal Tao Hui urged Wang Dao: "Strike before Su Jun arrives—cut the Fuling line and hold the Yangzi crossings at Dangli; we outnumber him and can settle this in one engagement."

sentences.zh: 若峻未至，可往逼其城。

translations.literal: If Jun has not arrived, one may go press his city.
translations.idiomatic: If his army has not yet marched out, push straight against his base."

sentences.zh: 今不先往，峻必先至。

translations.literal: Now if we do not go first, Jun will certainly arrive first.
translations.idiomatic: Delay, and Su Jun will reach the capital first."

sentences.zh: 先人有奪人之功，時不可失。

translations.literal: He who comes first has merit that snatches from others; the time cannot be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing the initiative wins the campaign—this moment will not come again."

sentences.zh: 」導然之。

translations.literal: " Dao approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao agreed.

sentences.zh: 庾亮以為峻脫徑來，是襲朝廷虛也，故計不行。

translations.literal: Yu Liang thought that if Jun took a shortcut coming, this was striking the court's emptiness; therefore the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang feared Su Jun might slip through by side roads and strike an undefended court, so the plan died.

sentences.zh: 峻遂破姑熟，取鹽米，亮方悔之。

translations.literal: Jun thereupon broke Gushu, took salt and rice, and Liang then regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun seized Gushu and its salt and grain stores before Yu Liang understood his mistake.

sentences.zh: 坦謂人曰：「觀峻之勢，必破台城。

translations.literal: Tan said to people: "Observing Jun's momentum, he will certainly break Taicheng."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan warned everyone: "Su Jun's momentum will carry him straight through Taicheng."

sentences.zh: 自非戰士，不須戎服。

translations.literal: Unless soldiers, need not martial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone not bound for battle should shed armor and travel as a civilian."

sentences.zh: 」既而台城陷，戎服者多死，白衣者無他，時人稱其先見。

translations.literal: Thereupon Taicheng fell; those in martial dress mostly died; those in white clothes had no other harm; people of the time praised his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When Taicheng fell, armored courtiers perished while civilians in plain clothes survived—everyone credited Kong Tan's foresight.

sentences.zh: 及峻挾天子幸石頭，坦奔陶侃，侃引為長史。

translations.literal: When Jun seized the Son of Heaven and went to Stone Fort, Tan fled to Tao Kan; Kan appointed him senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun dragged the emperor to Stone Fort, Kong Tan escaped to Tao Kan, who took him on as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時侃等夜築白石壘，至曉而成。

translations.literal: At that time Kan and others built White Stone fortress by night; by dawn it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's men threw up White Stone bastion overnight; by dawn it stood complete.

sentences.zh: 聞峻軍嚴聲，咸懼來攻。

translations.literal: Hearing Jun's army sound the alarm, all feared they would come attack.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun's drums threw everyone into panic—they expected an immediate assault.

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Tan said: "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan disagreed: "That is not what is happening."

sentences.zh: 若峻攻壘，必須東北風急，令我水軍不得往救。

translations.literal: If Jun attacks the fortress, northeast wind must be urgent, causing our water army unable to go rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun would need a howling northeaster to pin our fleet helpless if he meant to storm this fort."

sentences.zh: 今天清靜，賊必不動，決遣軍出江乘，掠京口以東矣。

translations.literal: Now heaven is clear and still; the bandits surely will not move; assuredly they dispatch troops out of Jiangcheng to raid east of Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The air is calm—the rebels will sit tight while detaching a column upriver from Jiangcheng to raid east of Jingkou."

sentences.zh: 」果如所籌。

translations.literal: " It turned out as planned.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as Kong Tan predicted.

sentences.zh: 時郗鑒鎮京口，侃等各以兵會。

translations.literal: At that time Xi Jian garrisoned Jingkou; Kan and others each brought troops to rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian held Jingkou while Tao Kan concentrated allied troops.

sentences.zh: 既至，坦議以為本不應須召郗公，遂使東門無限。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Tan debated that originally one should not have needed summon Duke Xi, thereby causing the eastern gate unlimited.
translations.idiomatic: Once assembled, Kong Tan argued they never should have summoned Duke Xi—doing so left the eastern approaches wide open.

sentences.zh: 今宜遣還，雖晚，猶勝不也。

translations.literal: Now one should dispatch him back; although late, still better than not.
translations.idiomatic: Send him back to his post—even now it beats leaving the flank bare."

sentences.zh: 侃等猶疑，坦固爭甚切，始令鑒還據京口，遣郭默屯大業，又令驍將李閎、曹統、周光與默並力，賊遂勢分，卒如坦計。

translations.literal: Kan and others still hesitated; Tan firmly argued very urgently; only then was Xi ordered back to hold Jingkou; Guo Mo was dispatched to garrison Daye; furthermore fierce generals Li Hong, Cao Tong, Zhou Guang were ordered with Mo to combine strength; the bandits thereby divided their momentum; in the end as Tan had planned.
translations.idiomatic: Although Tao Kan wavered, Kong Tan pressed relentlessly until Xi Jian returned to Jingkou, Guo Mo occupied Daye, and Li Hong, Cao Tong, and Zhou Guang reinforced him—splitting Su Jun's forces exactly as Kong Tan had intended.

sentences.zh: 及峻平，以坦為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: When Jun was pacified, Tan was appointed governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun fell, Kong Tan became governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 自陳吳多賢豪，而坦年少，未宜臨之。

translations.literal: He personally declared Wu has many worthy heroes, while Tan is young and not fit to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded that Wu swarmed with eminent families while he was too young to govern them.

sentences.zh: 王導、庾亮並欲用坦為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Wang Dao and Yu Liang both wished to employ Tan as governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao and Yu Liang both wanted to install him as governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時亂離之後，百姓凋弊，坦固辭之。

translations.literal: At that time after turmoil and separation the common people were withered and exhausted; Tan firmly declined it.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm shattered and the people destitute, Kong Tan firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 導等猶未之許。

translations.literal: Dao and others still did not permit him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao's faction refused to let him off.

sentences.zh: 坦慨然曰：「昔肅祖臨崩，諸君親據御床，共奉遺詔。

translations.literal: Tan sighed and said: "Formerly when Emperor Ming faced death, you gentlemen personally grasped the imperial couch and together upheld the testament."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan burst out: "When Emperor Ming lay dying, you ministers clustered at the imperial couch to receive his final edict."

sentences.zh: 孔坦疏賤，不在顧命之限。

translations.literal: Kong Tan is remote and base, not within the limits of entrusted mandate.
translations.idiomatic: I, Kong Tan, was too mean and remote to be counted among your fellowship of regents."

sentences.zh: 既有艱難，則以微臣為先。

translations.literal: Since there is hardship, then take your mean servant as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Now that crisis returns, you reach first for the insignificant man you once ignored."

sentences.zh: 今由俎上肉，任人膾截耳！

translations.literal: Now I am meat on the chopping block—others mince and slice at will!
translations.idiomatic: Today I am carcass on your board—slice me however you please!"

sentences.zh: 」乃拂衣而去。

translations.literal: " Then he brushed his robes and left.
translations.idiomatic: He swept his sleeves and walked out.

sentences.zh: 導等亦止。

translations.literal: Dao and others also stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao and his allies dropped the demand.

sentences.zh: 於是遷吳興內史，封晉陵男，加建威將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was transferred to interior governor of Wuxing, enfeoffed as baron of Jinling, added title as General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: They moved him to interior governor of Wuxing instead, with the title baron of Jinling and General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 以歲饑，運家米以振窮乏，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: Because of year famine, he transported household rice to relieve the poor and exhausted; the common people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck he shipped his own granary grain to feed the destitute, and the people depended on him.

sentences.zh: 時使坦募江淮流人為軍，有殿中兵，因亂東還，來應坦募，坦不知而納之。

translations.literal: At that time Tan was ordered to recruit wandering people of Jiang and Huai as troops; there were palace-army soldiers who because of turmoil returned east and came answering Tan's recruitment; Tan did not know and admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to draft refugees from the Huai and Yangzi valleys, Kong Tan unknowingly enlisted palace guards who had fled east amid the chaos.

sentences.zh: 或諷朝廷，以坦藏台叛兵，遂坐免。

translations.literal: Someone insinuated to the court that Tan harbored palace rebel troops; thereupon he was dismissed by sitting fault.
translations.idiomatic: Detractors told the court Kong Tan sheltered mutinous imperial troops, and he lost his post.

sentences.zh: 尋拜侍中。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 三康元年，石聰寇曆陽，王導為大司馬，討之，請坦為司馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sankan, Shi Cong raided Liyang; Wang Dao was grand marshal and campaigned against him; he requested Tan as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xiankang era (335 CE), Shi Cong struck Liyang; Grand Marshal Wang Dao took the field and named Kong Tan his army marshal.

sentences.zh: 會石勒新死，季龍專恣，石聰及譙郡太守彭彪等各遣使請降。

translations.literal: When Shi Le had newly died, Jilong acted arbitrarily; Shi Cong and Qiao commandery governor Peng Biao and others each sent envoys requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le had just died, leaving Shi Hu in charge; Shi Cong and Peng Biao of Qiao commandery each offered to defect.

sentences.zh: 坦與聰書曰：

translations.literal: Tan wrote to Cong saying:
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan sent Shi Cong this letter:

sentences.zh: 華狄道乖，南北回邈，瞻河企宋，每懷饑渴。

translations.literal: Hua and Di ways diverge; south and north turn remote; gazing at the River longing for Song—always cherishing hunger and thirst.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai River divides civilization from steppe folk; though north and south stand far apart, we gaze toward the Yellow River and ache for the Central Plains as thirst aches for water.

sentences.zh: 數會陽九，天禍晉國，奸凶猾夏，乘釁肆虐。

translations.literal: Repeatedly meeting yang nine, Heaven calamitized Jin state; villainous fierce ones ran riot through Xia, riding cracks to run rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Cycle after cycle of ill-starred years has scourged the Jin; traitors have exploited every crack to ravage the heartland.

sentences.zh: 我德雖衰，天命未改。

translations.literal: Our virtue although declining, Heaven's mandate has not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Our virtue may flag, yet Heaven's mandate still rests with Jin.

sentences.zh: 乾符啟再集之慶，中興應靈期之會，百六之艱既過，惟新之美日隆。

translations.literal: Qian's tally opens the blessing of gathering again; restoration responds to the conjunction of spirit period; the hardship of one hundred six having passed, only the beauty of renewal daily rises.
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic omens promise reunion; the restoration answers heaven's timetable—the worst calamities lie behind us, and renewal grows brighter daily.

sentences.zh: 而神州振盪，遺氓波散，誓命戎狄之手，局蹐豺狼之穴，朝廷每臨寐永歎，痛心疾首。

translations.literal: Yet the divine land quakes and shudders; surviving common folk scatter like waves; sworn to fate in barbarian hands, crouching in wolf dens—the court every time lying down sighs long, heartache to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the heartland still convulses; survivors cling to alien masters or cower in dens of wolves—every night the court groans awake, hearts cracked with grief.

sentences.zh: 天罰既集，罪人斯隕，王旅未加，自相魚肉。

translations.literal: Heaven's punishment having gathered, the guilty man thus falls; royal troops not yet applied, they eat one another like fish.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's axe already falls on the guilty, yet before our armies march Zhao devours Zhao.

sentences.zh: 豈非人怨神怒，天降其災！

translations.literal: Is it not that men resent and gods rage, Heaven sending down this calamity!
translations.idiomatic: Surely this is popular hatred and divine wrath—Heaven's scourge on traitors.

sentences.zh: 蘭艾同焚，賢愚所歎，哀矜勿喜，我後之仁，大赦曠廓，唯季龍是討。

translations.literal: Orchid and mugwort burn together—what worthies and fools lament; pity, do not rejoice—our later ruler's benevolence; great amnesty vast and broad—only Jilong is to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Good and wicked perish together—every honest man sorrows; our sovereign shows the mercy that mourns rather than gloats, grants sweeping amnesty to those willing to return, and reserves punishment for Shi Hu alone.

sentences.zh: 彭譙使至，粗具動靜，知將軍忿疾丑類，翻然同舉。

translations.literal: When Peng of Qiao's envoy arrived, roughly detailing movements, knowing the general detests the vile sort, turning alike raised together.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Biao's messenger reported your revulsion toward Shi Hu's clique and your readiness to rise with us.

sentences.zh: 承問欣豫，慶若在己。

translations.literal: Receiving the inquiry joyful and pleased, celebration as if in oneself.
translations.idiomatic: We rejoiced at the news as though the triumph were already ours.

sentences.zh: 何知幾之先覺，砎石之易悟哉！

translations.literal: How knowing the turning first awakens, splitting stone easy to comprehend!
translations.idiomatic: How keen your foresight—like striking flint, instantly understood!

sentences.zh: 引領來儀，怪無聲息。

translations.literal: Craning neck for coming ceremony, strange there is no sound or breath.
translations.idiomatic: We still crane our necks for your hostages and hear only silence—why?

sentences.zh: 將軍出自名族，誕育洪胄。

translations.literal: The general issues from a famous clan, born and raised in great lineage.
translations.idiomatic: You spring from a noble house and carry an eminent pedigree.

sentences.zh: 遭世多故，國傾家覆，生離親屬，假養異類。

translations.literal: Encountering the age's many troubles, state overturned family toppled, born separated from kin, foster-nurtured among alien kinds.
translations.idiomatic: War uprooted your clan and stranded you among barbarians who raised you as their own.

sentences.zh: 雖逼偽寵，將亦何賴！

translations.literal: Although compelled by false favor—what can one rely on!
translations.idiomatic: Their counterfeit favors bought your service—what loyalty could they deserve?

sentences.zh: 聞之者猶或有悼，況身嬰之，能不憤慨哉！

translations.literal: Those who hear still perhaps mourn—how much more those whose bodies undergo it—how not indignant!
translations.idiomatic: Listeners still pity your plight—how can you not rage while living it?

sentences.zh: 非我族類，其心必異，誠反族歸正之秋，圖義建功之日也。

translations.literal: Not our clan kind—their hearts surely differ; truly it is the autumn of returning clan to rectitude, the day of planning righteousness and establishing merit.
translations.idiomatic: Alien folk cannot share our hearts—now is the hour to return to your own blood and win glory for the cause.

sentences.zh: 若將軍喻納往言，宣之同盟，率關右之眾，輔河南之卒，申威趙魏，為國前驅，雖竇融之保西河，黥布之去項羽，比諸古今，未足為喻。

translations.literal: If the general enlightens and adopts previous words, proclaims them to covenant allies, leads the hosts west of the passes, aids the troops south of the River, extends might through Zhao and Wei, acts as vanguard for the state—even Dou Rong's guarding the western river, Qing Bu's leaving Xiang Yu—compared through ancient and modern, not enough to serve as analogy.
translations.idiomatic: Share this pledge with your allies, march from the Guanzhong heartland to join our Henan legions, sweep Zhao and Wei, and lead the van—your deed would dwarf Dou Rong's western stand or Qing Bu's break with Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 聖上寬明，宰輔弘納，雖射鉤之隙，賞之故行，雍齒之恨，侯之列國。

translations.literal: The sage lord is lenient and bright, chancellor broadly accepts—even arrow-hook enmity rewards past conduct, Yong Chi's hatred marquis among states.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign forgives freely—like Duke Huan honoring Guan Zhong despite an old arrow feud or Liu Bang ennobling Yong Chi despite ancient spite.

sentences.zh: 況二三子無曩人之嫌，而遇天啟之會，當如影響，有何遲疑！

translations.literal: Moreover you few lack former men's suspicion yet encounter Heaven's opening conjunction—should be like shadow and echo—what hesitation!
translations.idiomatic: You bear none of those old grudges—Heaven itself opens the door; answer it as shadow answers shape.

sentences.zh: 今六軍誡嚴，水陸齊舉，熊羆踴躍，齕噬爭先，鋒鏑一交，玉石同碎，雖復後悔，何嗟及矣！

translations.literal: Now the six armies strictly arrayed, water and land together raised, bear and brown leap, gnaw and bite striving first—points and arrowheads once crossed, jade and stone alike shatter—though again regret, how sigh and reach!
translations.idiomatic: Our hosts stand mobilized on land and river; once blades cross, good and wicked perish together—by then remorse will come too late.

sentences.zh: 僕以不才，世荷國寵，雖實不敏，誠為行李之主，區區之情，還信所具。

translations.literal: Your servant by lack of talent, generation bearing state favor—although truly not keen, truly am host of the envoy—petty feeling, return letter sets forth.
translations.idiomatic: Though unworthy, I inherit my family's offices and therefore steward this correspondence—every earnest word sits in the letter you hold.

sentences.zh: 夫機事不先，鮮不後悔，自求多福，唯將軍圖之。

translations.literal: As for critical affairs not first, seldom not afterward regret; seek blessing for yourself—only the general plan it.
translations.idiomatic: Miss the crucial moment and regret follows—seize your own fortune, General, while there is time.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遂不果北伐，人皆懷恨。

translations.literal: The court thereupon did not carry out northern campaign; people all harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The court failed to launch the northern expedition, and everyone resented it.

sentences.zh: 坦在職數年，遷侍中。

translations.literal: Tan in office several years was promoted to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After some years in office Kong Tan became palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時成帝每幸丞相王導府，拜導妻曹氏，有同家人，坦每切諫。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Cheng often visited Chancellor Wang Dao's residence, bowed to Dao's wife Lady Cao, as same as family members; Tan repeatedly sharply remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng constantly called at Wang Dao's mansion and treated Lady Cao like kin; Kong Tan remonstrated sharply each time.

sentences.zh: 時帝刻日納後，而尚書左僕射王彬卒，議者以為欲卻期。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had set a day to take the empress, but vice director of the left Wang Bin died; debaters thought this meant wishing to postpone the date.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had fixed his wedding day when Vice Director Wang Bin died—court gossips assumed the ceremony would slip.

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「婚禮之重，重於救日蝕。

translations.literal: Tan said: "The weight of wedding ritual is heavier than rescuing solar eclipse."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan said: "A royal wedding outweighs even the grand rite that stays a solar eclipse."

sentences.zh: 救日蝕，有後之喪，太子墮井，則止。

translations.literal: Rescuing solar eclipse—if there is later mourning, heir apparent falls in well—then stop.
translations.idiomatic: The eclipse ritual halts only for a queen's death or if the heir falls down a well—per the canon."

sentences.zh: 納後盛禮，豈可以臣喪而廢！

translations.literal: Taking empress great ritual—how can because of minister mourning abandon!
translations.idiomatic: You cannot scrap an empress's installation because a subject died!"

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: They followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 及帝既加元服，猶委政王導，坦每發憤，以國事為己憂，嘗從容言於帝曰：「陛下春秋以長，聖敬日躋，宜博納朝臣，諮諏善道。

translations.literal: When the emperor had already added capping dress, still entrusted government to Wang Dao; Tan repeatedly vented indignation, taking state affairs as personal worry; once calmly spoke to the emperor saying: "Your Majesty's years and seasons already grown, sagely reverence daily ascends—should broadly gather court ministers, consult good ways."
translations.idiomatic: Even after the capping ceremony Emperor Cheng left power with Wang Dao; Kong Tan burned with worry for the state and once urged him: "Your Majesty matures daily; widen counsel beyond one chancellor and seek the true Way of rule."

sentences.zh: 」由是忤導，出為廷尉，怏怏不悅，以疾去職。

translations.literal: Thereby offending Dao, he was sent out as commandant of justice, unhappy and displeased, resigned office due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao took offense and posted him commandant of justice; bitter and ill, Kong Tan soon resigned.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍，遷尚書，未拜。

translations.literal: He was added as palace attendant regular attendant and promoted to minister of the masters of writing; he did not assume the post.
translations.idiomatic: He received concurrent appointment as palace attendant regular attendant and nomination as minister of the masters of writing but never took up the latter office.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，庾冰省之，乃流涕。

translations.literal: When gravely ill, Yu Bing visited him; then shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: At death's door he received a visit from Yu Bing, who wept.

sentences.zh: 坦慨然曰：「大丈夫將終不問安國寧家之術，乃作兒女子相問邪！

translations.literal: Tan sighed and said: "When a great man nears his end he does not ask about arts that stabilize the state and pacify the household—instead he puts on the likeness of girls and boys questioning each other!"
translations.idiomatic: "Must a dying man sound like a fretful child?" Kong Tan snapped at Yu Bing. "Ask about the realm, not my bedside comfort!"

sentences.zh: 」冰深謝焉。

translations.literal: Bing deeply apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing withdrew, ashamed.

sentences.zh: 臨終，與庾亮書曰：「不謂疾苦，遂至頓弊，自省綿綿，奄忽無日。

translations.literal: Facing death, he wrote to Yu Liang saying: "I did not expect illness and suffering so to ruin me; examining myself I am drawn out thin; suddenly there are no days."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yu Liang a final letter: "I never thought sickness would waste me so; I fade away with imperial favor still unrepaid and ambitions untold—only regrets remain!"

sentences.zh: 修短命也，將何所悲！

translations.literal: " Xiū—short life—what is there to mourn!
translations.idiomatic: "Death comes soon enough—why indulge private grief?"

sentences.zh: 但以身往名沒，朝恩不報，所懷未敘，即命多恨耳！

translations.literal: " Only that body gone and name extinguished, court grace unrequited, what I harbored not narrated—many regrets at once departing fate!"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet my body will vanish before I repay the dynasty or voice half my aims—that rankles."

sentences.zh: 足下以伯舅之尊，居方伯之重，抗威顧眄，名震天下，榱椽之佐，常願下風。

translations.literal: " You, by uncle-on-the-mother's-side honor, occupy regional inspector's weight; raising awe with a glance, name shakes the world; as rafter-and-beam assistant I ever wished to stand below your wind."
translations.idiomatic: "You—imperial uncle—command a province and awe the realm; I long hoped merely to serve beneath your banner."

sentences.zh: 使九服式序，四海一統，封京觀于中原，反紫極于華壤，是宿昔之味詠，慷慨之本誠矣。

translations.literal: " Cause the nine garments to follow order, four seas unified, erect the burial mound of enemies on the Central Plain, return Purple Apex to splendid soil—this is what was tasted of old in verse, the root sincerity of generous fervor."
translations.idiomatic: "Restore ritual across the nine provinces, reunify the empire, raise victory monuments on the plain and bring the throne home to Luoyang—that was our shared dream."

sentences.zh: 今中道而斃，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: " Now midway dying—how not regrettable!"
translations.idiomatic: "To die halfway—how cruel!"

sentences.zh: 若死而有靈，潛聽風烈。

translations.literal: " If death yet has spirit, secretly listen to wind and fierce virtue."
translations.idiomatic: "If the dead still hear, witness what courage remains among us."

sentences.zh: 」俄卒，時年五十一。

translations.literal: " Shortly he died; at the time age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, fifty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 追贈光祿勳，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded superintendent of the imperial household; posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously named him superintendent of the imperial household and canonized him as "Simple" (Jian).

sentences.zh: 亮報書曰：「廷尉孔君，神遊體離，嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Liang replied in letter saying: "Commandant of Justice Kong—spirit roams body departed—alas alas!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang answered: "The commandant of justice—spirit flown, flesh abandoned—alas for him!"

sentences.zh: 得八月十五日書，知疾患轉篤，遂不起濟，悲恨傷楚，不能自勝。

translations.literal: " Receiving the fifteenth day of eighth month letter, knowing illness turned graver, thus cannot rise to aid—grief and resentment wound sorrow, cannot overcome myself."
translations.idiomatic: "Your letter of the fifteenth broke my heart—your decline is irreversible, and I cannot bear the grief."

sentences.zh: 足下方在中年，素少疾患，雖天命有在，亦禍出不圖。

translations.literal: " You were still in middle years, ordinarily few illnesses—although Heaven's mandate exists, also calamity issued unthought."
translations.idiomatic: "You were still in life's prime and seldom ill—Heaven's will may rule, yet this blow none foresaw."

sentences.zh: 且足下才經於世，世常須才，況於今日，倍相痛惜。

translations.literal: " Moreover your talent traverses the age; the age constantly needs talent—how much more today—doubly mutually grieved and treasured."
translations.idiomatic: "The age hungers for men of your caliber—your loss wounds doubly."

sentences.zh: 吾以寡乏，忝當大任，國恥未雪，夙夜憂憤。

translations.literal: " I by scant inadequacy shamefully bear great charge; state shame not yet washed—night and day anxious and resentful."
translations.idiomatic: "Feeble as I am, I shoulder the regency while northern shame still stains us—I burn with nightly rage."

sentences.zh: 常欲足下同在外籓，戮力時事。

translations.literal: " Constantly wished you together outside the screen, joining strength in current affairs."
translations.idiomatic: "I counted on you holding a frontier command so we might strike together."

sentences.zh: 此情未果，來書奄至。

translations.literal: " This feeling not yet fulfilled, incoming letter suddenly arrived."
translations.idiomatic: "That hope remains unmet—yet your farewell letter came."

sentences.zh: 申尋往復，不覺涕隕。

translations.literal: " Extending inquiry back and forth, unconsciously tears fall.
translations.idiomatic: "Reading line after line, tears blind me."

sentences.zh: 深明足下慷慨之懷，深痛足下不遂之志。

translations.literal: " Deeply understand your generous fervor's bosom, deeply grieve your unfulfilled will."
translations.idiomatic: "I feel the depth of your loyalty—and the sharper pain that you leave unfinished work."

sentences.zh: 邈然永隔，夫復何言！

translations.literal: " Remote indeed eternal separation—what more to say!"
translations.idiomatic: "We are parted forever—speech fails."

sentences.zh: 謹遣報答，並致薄祭，望足下降神饗之。

translations.literal: " Respectfully dispatch reply and moreover send thin sacrifice; hope you descend spirit and feast it."
translations.idiomatic: "I send this poor offering—may your spirit descend and partake."

sentences.zh: 」子混嗣。

translations.literal: His son Hun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kong Hun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 嚴字彭祖。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Pengzu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yan's courtesy name was Pengzu.

sentences.zh: 祖父奕，全椒令，明察過人。

translations.literal: Grandfather Yi was magistrate of Quanjiao—perceptive judgment surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kong Yi governed Quanjiao with uncanny discernment.

sentences.zh: 時有遺其酒者，始提入門，奕遙呵之曰：「人餉吾兩罌酒，其一何故非也？

translations.literal: Once someone lost wine and had just lifted it entering the gate; Yi from afar shouted at him: "Someone gifted me two jars of wine—why is one not so?"
translations.idiomatic: When a servant carried two jars through the gate, Kong Yi called out from across the yard that one vessel was false.

sentences.zh: 」檢視之，一罌果是水。

translations.literal: " Inspecting them, one jar indeed was water.
translations.idiomatic: Inspection proved one jar held water.

sentences.zh: 或問奕何以知之，笑曰：「酒重水輕，提酒者手有輕重之異故耳。

translations.literal: " Someone asked Yi how he knew; laughing he said: "Wine is heavy, water light—the wine-carrier's hands betray unequal weight."
translations.idiomatic: Asked how he knew, Kong Yi laughed: "Wine weighs more than water—the bearer's grip gave it away."

sentences.zh: 」在官有惠化，及卒，市人若喪慈親焉。

translations.literal: " In office he had kindly transformation; when he died, market people as if mourning kind parent.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate he ruled with kindness; when he died the townsfolk mourned like orphans.

sentences.zh: 父倫，黃門郎。

translations.literal: Father Lun was gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kong Lun served as gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 嚴少仕州郡，曆司徒掾、尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: Yan in youth served province and commandery; passed through aide to the Minister of Education and gentleman of the palace masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yan began in provincial posts, then became an aide to the Minister of Education and a gentleman of the palace masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 殷浩臨揚州，請為別駕。

translations.literal: When Yin Hao governed Yangzhou, he requested him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao recruited him as provincial aide when Yin governed Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Promoted to assistant director of the left of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant director of the left of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷崇樹浩，以抗擬桓溫，溫深以不平。

translations.literal: At that time the court elevated Hao to rival Huan Wen; Wen deeply considered it unfair.
translations.idiomatic: The court had built up Yin Hao to counter Huan Wen; Wen deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 浩又引接荒人，謀立功於閫外。

translations.literal: Hao further drew in frontier refugees, plotting to establish merit beyond the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao also recruited displaced northerners, hoping to win glory beyond the capital.

sentences.zh: 嚴言於浩曰：「當今時事艱難，可謂百六之運，使君屈己應務，屬當其會。

translations.literal: Yan spoke to Hao: "Present age affairs are difficult—may be called the fortune of one hundred six—make your lordship humble yourself responding to tasks—exactly meeting this conjunction."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yan warned Yin Hao: "These are ill-starred times—the court humbles itself for good reason."

sentences.zh: 聖懷所以日昃匪懈，臨朝斤斤，每欲深根固本，靜邊甯國耳，亦豈至私哉！

translations.literal: " The sage bosom therefore daily declines without slackness; facing court anxiously—always wishing deep roots and firm base, quiet borders and pacified state—how could it be utmost private!"
translations.idiomatic: "The sovereign toils from dawn to dusk to stabilize the realm—not for selfish ends!"

sentences.zh: 而處任者所志不同，所見各異，人口云云，無所不至。

translations.literal: " Yet those holding office—aspirations differ, views each different—people's mouths babbling—nothing not reached."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet every official nurses a private agenda, and rumor mongers invent anything."

sentences.zh: 頃來天時人情，良可寒心。

translations.literal: " Recently heaven's times and human feelings—truly can chill the heart."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven and public sentiment lately chill the blood."

sentences.zh: 古人為政，防人之口甚於防川。

translations.literal: " Ancients governing—guarding people's mouths more urgent than guarding rivers."
translations.idiomatic: "The ancients feared loose talk more than breached dikes."

sentences.zh: 間日侍座，亦已粗申所懷，不審竟當何以鎮之？

translations.literal: " Spare days attending seat—also already roughly declared what is harbored—do not examine finally how ought to calm it?"
translations.idiomatic: "We touched on this when I last sat with you—how will you quiet it?"

sentences.zh: 《老子》雲'夫唯不爭，則萬物不難與之爭'，此言不可不察也。

translations.literal: The Laozi reads: 'Only by not contending does none under Heaven find rivalry difficult with him'—this maxim demands reflection.
translations.idiomatic: The Laozi says, "Because he does not strive, nothing can strive against him"—ponder that.

sentences.zh: 愚意故謂朝廷宜更明授任之方，韓彭可專征伐，蕭曹守管籥，內外之任，各有攸司。

translations.literal: Your servant's meaning therefore considers the court should further clarify methods of appointment—Han Xin and Peng Yue may specialize in campaigns, Xiao He and Cao Shen guard the bolts—inner and outer tasks each have their office.
translations.idiomatic: Clarify who leads armies and who guards the capital—like Han general versus Xiao He at home.

sentences.zh: 深思廉藺屈申之道，平勃相和之義，令婉然通順，人無間言，然後乃可保大定功，平濟天下也。

translations.literal: Deeply ponder Lian Po and Lin Xiangru yielding or stretching; Ping and Bo harmonizing in alliance—order smoothly flowing—people without alien words—then afterward can preserve great and fix merit, level and aid All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Study how Lian and Lin traded humility and how Chen Ping worked with Zhou Bo—only harmony preserves the state.

sentences.zh: 又觀頃日降附之徒，皆人面獸心，貪而無親，難以義感。

translations.literal: " Moreover observing recent days those surrendering and attaching—all human faces beast hearts, greedy without kin—hard to move with righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: "The northern defectors you shelter wear human faces yet beast hearts—they understand no loyalty."

sentences.zh: 而聚著都邑，雜處人間，使君常疲聖體以接之，虛府庫以拯之，足以疑惑視聽耳。

translations.literal: " Yet gathering them in the capital, mixed dwelling among people—make your lordship constantly weary holy body receiving them, emptying granaries saving them—sufficient to confuse sight and hearing."
translations.idiomatic: "Herding them inside the walls drains your energy and treasury without earning trust."

sentences.zh: 」浩深納之。

translations.literal: " Hao deeply adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao took the rebuke to heart.

sentences.zh: 及哀帝踐阼，議所承統，時多異議。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai ascended the throne, they debated succession affiliation—at the time many divergent opinions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ai took the throne, ministers quarreled over his ritual lineage.

sentences.zh: 嚴與丹陽尹庾和議曰：「順本居正，親親不可奪，宜繼成皇帝。

translations.literal: Yan together with Yin He governor of Danyang debated: "Following root dwelling correct—close kin cannot be taken—ought to succeed Emperor Cheng."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yan and Yin He of Danyang urged enthroning Emperor Ai as heir to Emperor Cheng's line—the legally straightforward choice.

sentences.zh: 」諸儒咸以嚴議為長，竟從之。

translations.literal: " The scholars all considered Yan's debate superior; ultimately followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Classicists preferred Kong Yan's argument and the court adopted it.

sentences.zh: 隆和元年，詔曰：「天文失度，太史雖有禳祈之事，猶釁眚屢彰。

translations.literal: Longhe first year, edict said: "Astronomy missed measure—although grand clerk had averting prayer affairs—still omens repeatedly manifested."
translations.idiomatic: In Longhe 1 an edict blamed celestial disorder and lingering ill omens.

sentences.zh: 今欲依鴻祀之制，於太極殿前庭親執虔肅。

translations.literal: " Now wishing according to great-sacrifice system—in Supreme Ultimate hall front court personally hold reverent solemnity."
translations.idiomatic: "The throne proposes the ancient Hong sacrifice on the Taiji Hall forecourt."

sentences.zh: 」嚴諫曰：「鴻祀雖出《尚書大傳》，先儒所不究，歷代莫之興，承天接神，豈可以疑殆行事乎！

translations.literal: " Yan remonstrated: "Hong sacrifice although emerging from Documents Grand Tradition—former scholars did not investigate—successive dynasties none raised it—receiving Heaven connecting gods—how can one act on doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yan protested: "That rite appears only in the apocryphal *Great Tradition*—no dynasty performed it; dare we experiment with heaven?"

sentences.zh: 天道無親，唯德是輔，陛下祗順恭敬，留心兆庶，可以消災復異。

translations.literal: " Heaven's way without partiality—only virtue assists—your Majesty reverently comply respectful attentive—care for myriad multitude—can dissolve calamity restore anomaly."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven favors virtue alone—the emperor's diligence toward the people already answers heaven."

sentences.zh: 皆已蹈而行之，德合神明，丘禱久矣，豈須屈萬乘之尊，修雜祀之事！

translations.literal: " All already tread and practice—virtue matches spirits—Qi's prayer long—how need humble ten-thousands-carriage honor—repair miscellaneous sacrifice affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: "You walk every virtue Confucius prayed for at Qi—why stage ad hoc rituals beneath imperial dignity?"

sentences.zh: 君舉必書，可不慎歟！

translations.literal: " Lord's acts surely recorded—can one not be cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: "Historians record each imperial act—tread carefully!"

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉之而止。

translations.literal: " Emperor praised him and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Kong Yan and canceled the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 以為揚州大中正，嚴不就。

translations.literal: Appointed him Yangzhou grand impartial judge; Yan did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him Yangzhou's chief impartial judge; he declined.

sentences.zh: 有司奏免，詔特以侯領尚書

translations.literal: Relevant offices memorialized dismissal; edict specially ordered him as marquis to head the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Censors moved to strip him; an edict instead let him lead the masters of writing while keeping his marquis title.

sentences.zh: 時東海王奕求海鹽、錢塘以水牛牽埭稅取錢直，帝初從之，嚴諫乃止。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Donghai Yi requested Haiyan and Qiantang use water oxen to drag dyke tariffs collecting cash value—emperor at first followed—Yan remonstrated then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi wanted tolls on Haiyan and Qiantang dikes; Emperor Ai agreed until Kong Yan blocked it.
