sentences.zh: 初，帝或施私恩，以錢帛賜左右。

translations.literal: Earlier emperor sometimes applied private grace—using cash and silk to gift attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai had showered favorites with silk and coin.

sentences.zh: 嚴又啟諸所別賜及給廚食，皆應減省。

translations.literal: Yan again memorialized that various separate gifts and supplying kitchen food—all ought reduce and save.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yan urged cuts to those petty gifts and palace kitchen budgets.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「左右多困乏，故有所賜，今通斷之。

translations.literal: Emperor said: "Attendants mostly impoverished—therefore had gifts—now universally cut off."
translations.idiomatic: "My staff were destitute—that is why I gave alms," the emperor answered; "now stop all such gifts."

sentences.zh: 又廚膳宜有減撤，思詳具聞。

translations.literal: " Moreover kitchen meals ought have reduction and withdrawal—think carefully and fully report."
translations.idiomatic: "Trim the imperial kitchens as well—report every saving."

sentences.zh: 」嚴多所匡益。

translations.literal: " Yan many places corrected and benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yan's blunt counsel repeatedly improved court discipline.

sentences.zh: 太和中，拜吳興太守，加秩中二千石。

translations.literal: During Taihe era appointed governor of Wuxing—added salary rank two thousand shi median grade.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Taihe reign he became governor of Wuxing at two thousand shi median salary.

sentences.zh: 善於宰牧，甚得人和。

translations.literal: Skilled at shepherding—very obtained human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Wuxing so well that gentry and commoners alike embraced him.

sentences.zh: 余杭婦人經年荒，賣其子以活夫之兄子。

translations.literal: Yuhang woman—years of famine—sold her son to keep alive husband's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: A Yuhang woman, starving year after year, sold her child to save her nephew.

sentences.zh: 武康有兄弟二人，妻各有孕，弟遠行未反，遇荒歲，不能兩全，棄其子而活弟子。

translations.literal: Wukang had two brothers—wives each pregnant—younger brother traveled far not returned—met famine year—could not preserve both—discarded his son and preserved elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: In Wukang two brothers' wives bore sons in the same famine; the younger brother, away on travel, told his wife to abandon their infant so her nephew might live.

sentences.zh: 嚴並褒薦之。

translations.literal: Yan together praised and recommended them.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yan honored both families with commendations.

sentences.zh: 又甄賞才能之士，論者美焉。

translations.literal: Moreover distinguished and rewarded talented gentlemen—debators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He also elevated worthy locals—commentators applauded him.

sentences.zh: 五年，以疾去職，卒於家。

translations.literal: Fifth year due to illness resigned office—died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year illness forced retirement; he died at home.

sentences.zh: 三子：道民，宣城內史；

translations.literal: Three sons: Daomin—interior governor of Xuancheng;
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Daomin, interior governor of Xuancheng;

sentences.zh: 靜民，散騎侍郎；

translations.literal: Jingmin—gentleman cavalier attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Jingmin, gentleman cavalier attendant;

sentences.zh: 福民，太子洗馬，皆為孫恩所害。

translations.literal: Fumin—horse washer for heir apparent—all were harmed by Sun En.
translations.idiomatic: and Fumin, heir-apparent groom—all three fell victim to Sun En.

sentences.zh: 群字敬林，嚴叔父也。

translations.literal: Qun, courtesy name Jinglin—was Yan's younger paternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qun (courtesy Jinglin) was Kong Yan's uncle.

sentences.zh: 有智局，志尚不羈。

translations.literal: Had strategic perception—aspiration lofty unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He was shrewd and restless in ambition.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻入石頭，時匡術有寵於峻，賓從甚盛。

translations.literal: When Su Jun entered Stone Fort—at that time Kuang Shu had favor with Jun—guests and followers very abundant.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun seized Stone Fort, Kuang Shu basked in his favor with a crowd of hangers-on.

sentences.zh: 群與從兄愉同行于橫塘，遇之，愉止與語，而群初不視術。

translations.literal: Qun together with elder cousin Yu traveled at Hengtang—met him—Yu stopped and spoke with him—but Qun at first did not look at Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qun and Kong Yu met Kuang Shu at Hengtang; Yu exchanged pleasantries while Qun refused even to glance at him.

sentences.zh: 術怒，欲刃之。

translations.literal: Shu angry—wished to blade him.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang Shu drew steel to kill him.

sentences.zh: 愉下車抱術曰：「吾弟發狂，卿為我宥之。

translations.literal: Yu descended carriage embracing Shu saying: "My younger brother went mad—you for my sake forgive him."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yu leapt down and seized Kuang Shu's arms: "Forgive my crazed brother."

sentences.zh: 」乃獲免。

translations.literal: " Then obtained escape.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus did Kong Qun survive.

sentences.zh: 後峻平，王導保存術，嘗因眾坐，令術勸群酒，以釋橫塘之憾。

translations.literal: Later Jun pacified—Wang Dao preserved Shu—once because crowd seated ordered Shu urge Qun wine—to release Hengtang regret.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion Wang Dao sheltered Kuang Shu and tried to reconcile them over wine.

sentences.zh: 群答曰：「群非孔子，厄同匡人。

translations.literal: Qun replied saying: "Qun is not Confucius—hardship same as Kuang people."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qun answered: "I am no Confucius trapped among Kuang villagers."

sentences.zh: 雖陽和布氣，鷹化為鳩，至於識者，猶憎其目。

translations.literal: " Although yang harmony spreads qi—hawks transform into doves—as for those who recognize—still hate their eyes."
translations.idiomatic: "Warm winds may turn hawks into doves—yet anyone with eyes still despises a hawk's glare."

sentences.zh: 」導有愧色。

translations.literal: " Dao had ashamed color.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 仕歷中丞。

translations.literal: In office passed through censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，導嘗戒之曰：「卿恆飲，不見酒家覆瓿布，日月久糜爛邪？

translations.literal: Nature fond of wine—Dao once admonished him saying: "You constantly drink—do you not see wine-shop overturned jar cloth—sun moon long rotted?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao scolded his drinking: "Have you never seen the sodden sacks at a distillery?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「公不見肉糟淹更堪久邪？

translations.literal: " Replied saying: "Do you not see meat pickled in lees—more able endure long?"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qun shot back: "Marinades last longer than unwashed cloth."

sentences.zh: 」嘗與親友書云：「今年田得七百石秫米，不足了曲糵事。

translations.literal: " Once wrote to kin and friends saying: "This year fields obtained seven hundred shi of glutinous rice—not enough to finish yeast affairs."
translations.idiomatic: He boasted to kin that seven hundred shi of glutinous rice still could not slake his brewing.

sentences.zh: 」其耽湎如此。

translations.literal: " His drowning in wine thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his devotion to drink.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: Died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness.

sentences.zh: 嗣子沉。

translations.literal: Heir son Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His heir was Kong Chen.

sentences.zh: 沉字德度，有美名。

translations.literal: Chen, courtesy name Dedu—had fair reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chen (courtesy Dedu) enjoyed a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 何充薦沉于王導曰：「文思通敏，宜登宰門。

translations.literal: He Chong recommended Chen to Wang Dao saying: "Literary thought penetrating keen—ought ascend minister's gate."
translations.idiomatic: He Chong urged Wang Dao to recruit him: "His prose sparkles—promote him."

sentences.zh: 」辟丞相司徒掾、琅邪王文學，並不就。

translations.literal: " Summoned aide to Chancellor-of-State Minister of Education and Langye prince literary attendant—both did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao offered posts as Chancellor aide and tutor to the Prince of Langye—Kong Chen refused both.

sentences.zh: 從兄坦以裘遺之，辭不受。

translations.literal: Elder cousin Tan by fur coat gifted him—declined not accepting.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Kong Tan sent a fur robe; Kong Chen returned it.

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「晏平仲儉，祀其先人，豚肩不掩豆，猶狐裘數十年，卿復何辭！

translations.literal: Tan said: "Yan Pingzhong frugal—sacrificing his ancestors—pig shoulder did not cover dou—still fox fur several tens years—you again what decline!"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan teased him: "Yan Ying wore one fox robe for decades—take the coat!"

sentences.zh: 」於是受而服之。

translations.literal: Then he accepted and wore it.
translations.idiomatic: He relented and wore the robe.

sentences.zh: 是時沉與魏顗、虞球、虞存、謝奉並為四族之俊。

translations.literal: At that time Chen together with Wei Yi, Yu Qiu, Yu Cun, Xie Feng were altogether celebrated four-clans talents.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chen ranked with Wei Yi, Yu Qiu, Yu Cun, and Xie Feng among the foremost noble heirs.

sentences.zh: 沉子廞，位至吳興太守、廷尉。

translations.literal: Chen's son Yin rose to interior governor of Wuxing and commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin became governor of Wuxing and commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 廞子琳之，以草書擅名，又為吳興太守，侍中。

translations.literal: Yin's son Linzhi—by cursive hand script famed—also served as interior governor of Wuxing and palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son Linzhi won fame for cursive calligraphy and likewise governed Wuxing and entered the palace corps.

sentences.zh: 丁潭，字世康，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Ding Tan, courtesy name Shikang, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Tan (courtesy Shikang) came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖固，吳司徒。

translations.literal: Grandfather Gu was Minister of Education under Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ding Gu had been Wu's Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 父彌，梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Father Mi was regional inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ding Mi governed Liangzhou as regional inspector.

sentences.zh: 潭初為郡功曹，察孝廉，除郎中，稍遷丞相西閣祭酒。

translations.literal: Tan at first was commandery clerk for merit, inspected filial and incorrupt, appointed gentleman of the palace, gradually promoted overseer of sacrifices at the Chancellor's western pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as commandery merit clerk, passed filial-and-incorrupt rating, became a gentleman of the palace, then overseer of sacrifices at the western pavilion of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時元帝稱制，使各陳時事損益，潭上書曰：

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Emperor held provisional rule—ordered each to state current affairs' harm and benefit—Tan submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: While Yuan Emperor ruled in name alone he solicited policy critiques; Ding Tan submitted:

sentences.zh: 為國者恃人須才，蓋二千石長吏是也。

translations.literal: "Those who hold the state rely on men needing talent—nothing less than two-thousand-shi chief magistrates."
translations.idiomatic: "No institution matters more than picking sound governors."

sentences.zh: 安可不明簡其才，使必允當。

translations.literal: "How can one not clearly sort their talents—making sure appointments fit?"
translations.idiomatic: "Scrutinize candidates until every seat fits its officer."

sentences.zh: 既然得其人，使久於其職，在官者無苟且，居下者有恆心，此為政之較也。

translations.literal: "Once you obtain the right men—keep them long in post—then officeholders avoid slack conduct and subordinates maintain steadfast hearts—this is the yardstick of governance."
translations.idiomatic: "Stable tenure breeds conscientious magistrates and loyal subjects—that is sound administration."

sentences.zh: 今之長吏，遷轉既數，有送迎之費。

translations.literal: "Present chief magistrates rotate so often there are farewell and welcome expenses."
translations.idiomatic: "Constant transfers waste wealth on endless send-offs."

sentences.zh: 古人三載考績，三考黜陟，中才處局，故難以速成矣。

translations.literal: "The ancients examined merit once every three years—after three reviews promoted or demoted—men of middling talent in office therefore hard to achieve rapid completion."
translations.idiomatic: "Ancient rule reviewed governors triennially; middling officials need years to show results."

sentences.zh: 夫兵所以防禦未然，鎮壓奸凶，周雖三聖，功成由武。

translations.literal: "Armies exist to guard against what is not yet manifest—to suppress villainous fierce ones—though Zhou had three sages—achievement completed through martial force."
translations.idiomatic: "Armies deter rebellion—Zhou's sage kings prevailed through arms as well as rites."

sentences.zh: 今戎戰之世，益宜留心，簡選精銳，以備不虞。

translations.literal: "Now in age of martial warfare—still more should one attend mind—select and pick crack troops—to prepare against unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: "In wartime train elite soldiery before disaster strikes."

sentences.zh: 無事則優其身，有難則責其力。

translations.literal: "Without affairs then nurture their persons—with difficulty then demand their strength."
translations.idiomatic: "Pay soldiers in peace so they fight when crisis comes."

sentences.zh: 竊聞今之兵士，或私有役使，而營陳不充。

translations.literal: "Privately heard today's soldiers—some privately deployed—yet camps and formations not filled."
translations.idiomatic: "Commanders press troops into private labor while formations stand hollow."

sentences.zh: 夫為國者，由為家也。

translations.literal: "Those who hold the state—it is like managing a household."
translations.idiomatic: "Ruling a realm resembles balancing a household budget."

sentences.zh: 計財力之所任，審趨舍之舉動，不營難成之功，損棄分外之役。

translations.literal: "Calculate what finance and strength can bear—examine advance and retreat's movement—do not operate achievements hard to complete—discard labor beyond allotted share."
translations.idiomatic: "Spend only what revenue allows; abandon wasteful campaigns."

sentences.zh: 今兵人未強，當審其宜，經塗遠舉，未獻大捷，更使力單財盡而威望挫弱也。

translations.literal: "Now soldiers not yet strong—should examine what is fitting—distant campaigns not yet presenting great victory—only make strength thin resources exhausted and martial prestige weakened."
translations.idiomatic: "Ill-trained armies cannot endure futile expeditions—they drain silver and morale."

sentences.zh: 及帝踐阼，拜駙馬都尉、奉朝請、尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: When emperor ascended the throne—appointed chief commandant of attendant cavalry—court attendant—gentleman of the masters of writing bureau of sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At Ming Emperor's accession Ding Tan took chief commandant of attendant cavalry, court status, and the sacrifices bureau.

sentences.zh: 時琅邪王裒始受封，帝欲引朝賢為其國上卿，將用潭，以問中書令賀循。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Langye Shou first received investiture—emperor wished to draw court worthies as his state's senior minister—about to use Tan—therefore asked Director of the Palace Secretariat He Xun.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shou of Langye needed a chief minister, the throne favored Ding Tan and consulted He Xun.

sentences.zh: 循曰：「郎中令職望清重，實宜審授。

translations.literal: Xun said: "Superintendent of the Household's office—duty and prestige pure and weighty—truly should examine appointment."
translations.idiomatic: He Xun replied: "The prince's superintendent must be chosen with extreme care."

sentences.zh: 潭清淳貞粹，雅有隱正，聖明所簡，才實宜之。

translations.literal: "Tan pure honest chaste pure—elegantly possesses hidden rectitude—what sagely clarity selects—talent truly fits it."
translations.idiomatic: "Ding Tan's integrity suits the post perfectly."

sentences.zh: 」遂為琅邪王郎中令。

translations.literal: " Thereupon became Langye prince superintendent of the household.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Tan received the Langye prince's superintendent post.

sentences.zh: 會裒薨，潭上疏求行終喪禮，曰：「在三之義，禮有達制，近代已來，或隨時降殺，宜一匡革，以敦於後，輒案令文，王侯之喪，官僚服斬，既葬而除。

translations.literal: When Shou died—Tan submitted memorial requesting to perform final mourning rites—saying: "The meaning of serving three—rites allow overruling systems—in recent ages sometimes following times lowering degrees—ought uniformly reform—to urge posterity—according to statute text—princes and marquises' mourning—bureaucrats wear chopped hemp—after burial remove."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shou died, Ding Tan asked to observe full mourning, citing statutes on princely funerals.

sentences.zh: 今國無繼統，喪庭無主，臣實陋賤，不足當重，謬荷首任，禮宜終喪。

translations.literal: " Now state lacks continuing succession—mourning court lacks master—your servant truly base and low—not sufficient to bear weight—wrongly burdened first office—by rites ought complete mourning."
translations.idiomatic: "With no heir yet enthroned I alone lead the prince's household—I must finish the three-year rites."

sentences.zh: 」詔下博議。

translations.literal: " Edict descended broad debate.
translations.idiomatic: The court referred his plea for debate.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒杜夷議：「古者諒闇，三年不言。

translations.literal: National University overseer Du Yi debated: "In antiquity concealment—three years not speaking."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi cited ancient palace seclusion during mourning.

sentences.zh: 下及周世，稅衰效命。

translations.literal: " Down to Zhou era—remove coarse hemp and answer summons."
translations.idiomatic: By Zhou times mourning hemp yielded to duty.

sentences.zh: 春秋之時，天子諸侯既葬而除。

translations.literal: " Spring and Autumn age—Son of Heaven and feudal lords after burial remove."
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn records show rulers shedding mourning after burial.

sentences.zh: 此所謂三代損益，禮有不同。

translations.literal: " This is called Three Dynasties' diminishment and increase—rites having differences."
translations.idiomatic: Thus three dynasties adjusted mourning by circumstance.

sentences.zh: 故三年之喪，由此而廢。

translations.literal: " Therefore three-year mourning—for this reason abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Hence full three-year mourning fell away for rulers.

sentences.zh: 然則漢文之詔，合于隨時，凡有國者，皆宜同也，非唯施於帝皇而已。

translations.literal: " Then Han Wendi's edict accorded with following times—every state-holder ought alike—not only applied to emperors."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han shortened mourning appropriately—every prince should follow suit.

sentences.zh: 案禮，殤與無後，降于成人。

translations.literal: " According to rites—youth-deaths and without heirs—lower than adults."
translations.idiomatic: Rites shorten mourning for childless or youthful deaths.

sentences.zh: 有後，既葬而除。

translations.literal: " Having heirs—after burial remove."
translations.idiomatic: When an heir survives, mourning ends at burial.

sentences.zh: 今不得以無後之故而獨不除也。

translations.literal: " Now cannot because without heir reason alone not remove."
translations.idiomatic: You cannot prolong mourning merely because no heir survives.

sentences.zh: 愚以丁郎中應除衰麻，自宜主祭，以終三年。

translations.literal: " Your servant considers Superintendent Ding ought remove coarse hemp—personally ought preside sacrifices—to complete three years."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi felt Ding Tan should shed officials' mourning yet host rites for three years.

sentences.zh: 」太常賀循議：「禮，天子諸侯俱以至尊臨人，上下之義，群臣之禮，自古以來，其例一也。

translations.literal: " Minister of Ceremonies He Xun debated: "Rites—Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike use utmost honor facing people—high and low righteousness—hosts and ministers' rites—from ancient to present—the example is one."
translations.idiomatic: He Xun argued sovereign and vassal mourning must align.

sentences.zh: 故禮盛則並全其重，禮殺則從其降。

translations.literal: " Therefore when rites grand then together preserve its weight—when rites reduced then follow lowering."
translations.idiomatic: Grand occasions demand full observance; lesser ones may yield.

sentences.zh: 春秋之事，天子諸侯不行三年。

translations.literal: " Spring and Autumn affairs—Son of Heaven and feudal lords do not practice three years."
translations.idiomatic: Annals never show feudal lords keeping three full years.

sentences.zh: 至於臣為君服，亦宜以君為節，未有君除而臣服，君服而臣除者。

translations.literal: " As for ministers serving ruler—also ought take ruler as measure—none where ruler removes and minister serves—ruler serves and minister removes."
translations.idiomatic: Subjects cannot out-mourn their lord or shed grief while he still mourns.

sentences.zh: 今法令，諸侯卿相官屬為君斬衰，既葬而除。

translations.literal: " Present statute law—feudal lords' ministers and aides for ruler chopped hemp—after burial remove."
translations.idiomatic: Current code ends ministerial mourning at the prince's burial.

sentences.zh: 以令文言之，明諸侯不以三年之喪與天子同可知也。

translations.literal: " By statute text speaking—clear feudal lords do not use three-year mourning same as Son of Heaven—knowable."
translations.idiomatic: Statute explicitly distinguishes princes from the emperor.

sentences.zh: 君若遂服，則臣子輕重無應除者也。

translations.literal: " If lord indeed wears mourning—then ministers and sons heavy light none responding removal."
translations.idiomatic: If the prince stays in hemp, no minister may lighten dress alone.

sentences.zh: 若當皆除，無一人獨重之文。

translations.literal: " If ought all remove—none one person alone heavy text."
translations.idiomatic: If everyone doffs mourning, no lone heavier obligation remains.

sentences.zh: 禮有攝主而無攝重，故大功之親主人喪者，必為之再祭練祥，以大功之服，主人三年喪者也。

translations.literal: " Rites have substitute host but no substitute heaviness—therefore close kin of great merit hosting lord's mourning—must for them perform secondary lintel and auspicious sacrifices—in great merit's dress—host is one observing three-year mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual allows a stand-in host but not a stand-in chief mourner—great-kin substitutes preside second-grade rites.

sentences.zh: 苟謂諸侯與天子同制，國有嗣王，自不全服，而人主居喪，素服主祭，三年不攝吉事，以尊令制。

translations.literal: " If suppose feudal lords same system as Son of Heaven—state having heir-apparent—not personally full mourning—yet lord dwelling mourning—plain dress presiding sacrifices—three years not assuming auspicious affairs—to honor statute system."
translations.idiomatic: If princes matched the throne, regents would wear white yet leave state business—but statutes forbid that confusion.

sentences.zh: 若當遠跡三代，令復舊典，不依法令者，則侯之服貴賤一例，亦不得唯一人論。

translations.literal: " If ought trace far Three Dynasties—order restore old canons—not following statute law—then marquises' dress noble base same pattern—also cannot only one person debate."
translations.idiomatic: Unless reviving antiquity wholesale, noble mourners must follow one rule.

sentences.zh: 」於是詔使除服，心喪三年。

translations.literal: " Thereupon edict ordered remove hemp garments—heart mourning three years.
translations.idiomatic: An edict traded sackcloth for inner grief lasting three years.

sentences.zh: 太興三年，遷王導驃騎司馬，轉中書郎，出為廣武將軍、東陽太守，以清潔見稱。

translations.literal: Taixing third year—promoted Wang Dao's marshal for grand commander of cavalry—shifted gentleman of the palace secretariat—went out as General Who Extends Might and interior governor of Dongyang—by purity praised.
translations.idiomatic: In Taixing 3 he served Wang Dao as cavalry marshal, then palace secretary, then governor of Dongyang—celebrated for honesty.

sentences.zh: 徵為太子左衛率，不拜。

translations.literal: Summoned as commander of the left guards for the heir—did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined appointment as captain of the heir's left guards.

sentences.zh: 成帝踐阼，以為散騎常侍、侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng ascended—appointed palace attendant regular attendant and palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng he joined the palace attendant corps.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻作亂，帝蒙塵於石頭，唯潭及侍中鐘雅、劉超等隨從不離帝側。

translations.literal: When Su Jun raised turmoil—emperor suffered dust at Stone Fort—only Tan together with palace attendants Zhong Ya, Liu Chao and others followed never leaving emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun's coup Ding Tan stayed with Emperor Cheng at Stone Fort alongside Zhong Ya and Liu Chao.

sentences.zh: 峻誅，以功賜爵永安伯，遷大尚書，徙廷尉，累遷左光祿大夫、領國子祭酒、本國大中正，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Jun executed—by merit granted noble rank Yongan bo—promoted senior minister of masters of writing—shifted commandant of justice—promoted in stages senior grand master of the left, overseer of National University, grand impartial judge of home commandery, added palace attendant regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun fell Ding Tan earned the Yongan barony, rose through senior minister, commandant of justice, grand master, university overseer, and chief impartial judge.

sentences.zh: 康帝即位，屢表乞骸骨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Kang ascended, he repeatedly memorialized begging to surrender his bones.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Kang took the throne, Ding Tan repeatedly asked permission to retire.

sentences.zh: 詔以光祿大夫還第，門施行馬，祿秩一如舊制，給傳詔二人，賜錢二十萬，床帳褥席。

translations.literal: Edict ordered him grand master of rank returning to mansion—gate erecting horse-blocks—salary ranks entirely as old system—grant two edict couriers—gift twenty thousand cash—bed curtains mats cushions.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as grand master with full salary, carriage blocks at his gate, two runners, twenty thousand cash, and bedding gifts.

sentences.zh: 年八十，卒。

translations.literal: Age eighty—died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，大夫如故，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded palace attendant—grand master as before—posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously honored as palace attendant and canonized "Simple."

sentences.zh: 王導嘗謂孔敬康有公才而無公望，丁世康有公望而無公才。

translations.literal: Wang Dao once said Kong Jingkang had ducal talent but lacked ducal renown—Ding Shikang had ducal renown but lacked ducal talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao quipped that Kong Yu had ministerial ability without prestige, Ding Tan prestige without equal ability.

sentences.zh: 子話，位至散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Son Hua rose to gentleman cavalier attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ding Hua reached gentleman cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 張茂，字偉康，少單貧，有志行，為鄉里所敬信。

translations.literal: Zhang Mao, courtesy name Weikang—in youth orphaned and poor—had aspiration and conduct—by village esteemed and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao (courtesy Weikang) grew up poor yet principled and trusted locally.

sentences.zh: 初起義兵，討賊陳斌，一郡用全。

translations.literal: First raised righteous troops—campaigning against bandit Chen Bin—one commandery thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He raised militia against Chen Bin and saved his commandery.

sentences.zh: 元帝辟為掾屬。

translations.literal: Yuan Emperor summoned him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Emperor recruited him as staff.

sentences.zh: 官有老牛數十，將賣之，茂曰：「殺牛有禁，買者不得輒屠，齒力疲老，又不任耕駕，是以無用之物收百姓利也。

translations.literal: Office had several tens old oxen—about to sell them—Mao said: "Killing oxen forbidden—buyers cannot casually butcher—teeth strength weary old—also cannot bear plow harness—therefore useless thing collecting common people's profit."
translations.idiomatic: When magistrates tried to sell aging oxen, Zhang Mao protested that useless livestock still could not be butchered under law.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor canceled the sale.

sentences.zh: 遷太子右衛率，出補吳興內史。

translations.literal: Promoted commander of right guards for heir—went out supplemented interior governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He became captain of the heir's right guards, then governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 沈充之反也，茂與三子並遇害。

translations.literal: When Shen Chong rebelled—Mao together with three sons together met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong's revolt cost Zhang Mao and his three sons their lives.

sentences.zh: 茂弟盎，為周劄將軍，充討劄，盎又死之。

translations.literal: Mao's younger brother Ang—was Zhou Zha's general—Chong campaigned against Zha—Ang again died for it.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Ang served Zhou Zha against Shen Chong and died in that fight.

sentences.zh: 贈茂太僕。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded superintendent of carriages.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously named him superintendent of carriages.

sentences.zh: 茂少時夢得大象，以問占夢萬推。

translations.literal: Mao in youth dreamed obtaining elephant—thereupon asked dream-diviner Wan Tui.
translations.idiomatic: Young Zhang Mao dreamed of an elephant and consulted Wan Tui.

sentences.zh: 推曰：「君當為大郡，而不善也。

translations.literal: Tui said: "Lord ought become great commandery—but not auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Wan Tui said a great governorship awaited—but ill-starred.

sentences.zh: 」問其故，推曰：「象者大獸，獸者守也，故知當得大郡。

translations.literal: " Asked the reason—Tui said: "Elephant is great beast—beasts mean guarding—therefore know ought obtain great commandery."
translations.idiomatic: "Elephants mean weighty office," Wan explained.

sentences.zh: 然象以齒焚，為人所害。

translations.literal: " Yet elephant by tusks burns—therefore harmed by people."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet ivory destroys the elephant—you will die by men."

sentences.zh: 」果如其言。

translations.literal: " Indeed as his words.
translations.idiomatic: The omen came true to the last word.

sentences.zh: 陶回，丹陽人也。

translations.literal: Tao Hui—man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hui came from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 祖基，吳交州刺史。

translations.literal: Grandfather Ji was regional inspector of Jiao for Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tao Ji held Jiao province under Wu.

sentences.zh: 父抗，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Father Kang was junior mentor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao Kang served as junior mentor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 回辟司空府中軍、主簿，並不就。

translations.literal: Hui summoned to Minister of Education headquarters central army and chief clerk—both did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He spurned posts in the Minister of Education's army staff.

sentences.zh: 大將軍王敦命為參軍，轉州別駕。

translations.literal: Grand General Wang Dun ordered him army adviser—shifted commandery administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun made him army adviser, then provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 敦死，司徒王導引為從事中郎，遷司馬。

translations.literal: When Dun died—Minister of Education Wang Dao led him as executive aide—promoted marshal.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun died Wang Dao brought him in as executive aide and marshal.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之役，回與孔坦言於導，請早出兵守江口，語在坦傳。

translations.literal: During Su Jun campaign—Hui together with Kong Tan reported to Dao—requesting early dispatch troops guard river mouth—words in Tan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: As Su Jun advanced, Tao Hui and Kong Tan urged Wang Dao to hold the river mouth—Kong Tan's biography records it.

sentences.zh: 峻將至，回復謂亮曰：「峻知石頭有重戍，不敢直下，必向小丹陽南道步來，宜伏兵要之，可一戰而擒。

translations.literal: When Jun was about to arrive—Hui again said to Liang: "Jun knows Stone Fort has heavy garrison—does not dare go straight down—must go by Lesser Danyang southern road on foot—ought lay ambush awaiting—can one battle and capture."
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hui warned Yu Liang that Su Jun would skirt Stone Fort via Lesser Danyang—lay ambush there.

sentences.zh: 」亮不從。

translations.literal: " Liang did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang ignored him.

sentences.zh: 峻果由小丹陽經秣陵，迷失道，逢郡人，執以為鄉導。

translations.literal: " Jun indeed came by Lesser Danyang through Moling—lost road—met commandery man—seized him as village guide.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun took Lesser Danyang, lost his way near Moling, and pressed a local guide.

sentences.zh: 時峻夜行，甚無部分。

translations.literal: " At that time Jun marched by night—very without discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun's night march was chaotic.

sentences.zh: 亮聞之，深悔不從回等之言。

translations.literal: " Liang hearing deeply regretted not following Hui and others' words.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang bitterly regretted spurning Tao Hui's advice.

sentences.zh: 尋王師敗績，回還本縣，收合義軍，得千餘人，並為步軍，與陶侃、溫嶠等並力攻峻，又別破韓晁，以功封康樂伯。

translations.literal: " Shortly imperial armies defeated—Hui returned native county—gathered righteous army—obtained over one thousand—all infantry—together with Tao Kan, Wen Qiao et al combined attacked Jun—also separately broke Han Chao—by merit enfeoffed baron of Kangle.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout Tao Hui rallied a thousand foot soldiers, fought beside Tao Kan and Wen Qiao, crushed Han Chao, and earned the Kangle barony.

sentences.zh: 時大賊新平，綱維弛廢，司徒王導以回有器幹，擢補北軍中候，俄轉中護軍。

translations.literal: " At time great bandits newly pacified—nets and cords lax waste—Minister of Education Wang Dao because Hui had vessel capacity—promoted supplemented northern army middle inspector—shortly shifted Defender-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: With peace fragile Wang Dao named Tao Hui northern army inspector then Defender-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷征虜將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: " After long time promoted General Who Subdues Barbarians—interior governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he governed Wuxing as General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 時人饑谷貴，三吳尤甚。

translations.literal: " At time people starved grain costly—Three Wu especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Famine made grain ruinously costly in the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 詔欲聽相鬻賣，以拯一時之急。

translations.literal: " Edict wished permit mutual selling—to relieve moment's urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The court prepared to legalize child-sale to stem starvation.

sentences.zh: 回上疏曰：「當今天下不普荒儉，唯獨東土穀價偏貴，便相鬻賣，聲必遠流，北賊聞之，將窺疆場。

translations.literal: " Hui submitted memorial: "Present realm not universally famine—only eastern lands grain price overly dear—if mutual selling—reputation surely flows far—northern bandits hearing—will spy borders."
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hui argued that legalizing human trafficking would advertise Jin weakness to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 如愚臣意，不如開倉廩以振之。

translations.literal: " Like foolish servant's meaning—better open granaries to relieve them."
translations.idiomatic: "Open state granaries instead," he pleaded.

sentences.zh: 」乃不待報，輒便開倉，及割府郡軍資數萬斛米以救乏絕，由是一境獲全。

translations.literal: " Then without awaiting reply—without authorization opened granaries—and cut prefectural military supplies several tens thousand hu rice to rescue exhaustion—thereby one territory wholly preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting he opened granaries and poured tens of thousands of hu into Wu—the district survived.

sentences.zh: 既而下詔，並敕會稽、吳郡依回振恤，二郡賴之。

translations.literal: " Afterward edict descended—and ordered Kuaiji and Wu commanderies follow Hui's relief—two commanderies relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial orders extended his policy to Kuaiji and Wu.

sentences.zh: 在郡四年，徵拜領軍將軍，加散騎常侍，征虜將軍如故。

translations.literal: " In commandery four years—summoned appointed General Who Leads Army—added palace attendant regular attendant—General Who Subdues Barbarians as before.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he became General Who Leads the Army with prior titles intact.

sentences.zh: 回性雅正，不憚強禦。

translations.literal: " Hui nature elegant upright—not fearing strong oppression.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hui combined integrity with iron nerve.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹桓景佞事王導，甚為導所昵。

translations.literal: " Danyang governor Huan Jing flattered Duke Wang Dao—very favored by Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Huan Jing curried Wang Dao's favor shamelessly.

sentences.zh: 回常慷慨謂景非正人，不宜親狎。

translations.literal: Hui often generously declared Jing was not upright man—not fit to draw intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hui insisted Huan Jing was no gentleman and unworthy of intimacy.

sentences.zh: 會熒惑守南斗經旬，導語回曰：「南斗，揚州分，而熒惑守之，吾當遜位以厭此謫。

translations.literal: When Mars guarded Southern Dipper full ten days—Dao said to Hui: "Southern Dipper—Yangzhou's division—and Mars guards it—I ought yield position to suppress this reproach."
translations.idiomatic: When Mars lingered over Sagittarius Wang Dao told Tao Hui he would resign to appease heaven.

sentences.zh: 」回答曰：「公以明德作相，輔弼聖主，當親忠貞，遠邪佞，而與桓景造膝，熒惑何由退舍！

translations.literal: " Hui replied: "You by bright virtue act chancellor—aiding sagely lord—ought draw near loyal purity—distance wicked flattery—yet with Huan Jing knee-to-knee—how could Mars thereby withdraw lodging!"
translations.idiomatic: "Your virtue anchors the court," Tao Hui retorted; "banish flatterers—do not blame the planets."

sentences.zh: 」導深愧之咸和二年，以疾辭職，帝不許。

translations.literal: " Dao deeply ashamed of it. Xianhe second year—due to illness resigned office—emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao flushed with shame. In Xianhe 2 Tao Hui begged sick leave; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 徙護軍將軍，常侍、領軍如故，未拜，卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: Transferred Defender-in-Chief—regular attendant—General Who Leads Army as before—not invested—died—age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Named Defender-in-Chief while keeping prior titles, he died at fifty-one before inauguration.

sentences.zh: 諡曰威。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Canonized as "Formidable" (Wei).

sentences.zh: 四子：汪、陋、隱、無忌。

translations.literal: Four sons: Wang, Lou, Yin, Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: He left four sons—Wang, Lou, Yin, and Wuji.

sentences.zh: 汪嗣爵，位至輔國將軍、宣城內史，陋冠軍將軍，隱少府，無忌光祿勳，兄弟咸有于用。

translations.literal: Wang succeeded noble rank—rose to General Who Aids the State and interior governor of Xuancheng—Lou champion general—Yin minister of the lesser treasury—Wuji superintendent of the imperial household—brothers all had administrative usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang inherited his rank and reached general of state support and Xuancheng; Lou became champion general; Yin headed the lesser treasury; Wuji became superintendent of the household—each proved capable.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孔愉父子暨丁潭等，咸以筱簜之材，邀締構之運，策名霸府，騁足高衢，曆試清階，遂登顯要，外宣政績，內盡謀猷，罄心力以佐時，竭股肱以衛主，並能保全名節，善始令終。

translations.literal: Historian's remark: Kong Yu father-and-sons together with Ding Tan and others—all by bamboo-slip timber's talent—invited founding-structure's fortune—registered name at overlord headquarters—galloping feet on high avenues—successively tested pure ranks—thereupon ascended eminent essentials—outside proclaimed administrative merit—inside exhausted stratagem plans—exhausting heart strength to aid times—draining thigh and arm to guard lord—and able preserve intact name and integrity—good beginning commanded end.
translations.idiomatic: The historians observe that Kong Yu, his sons, Ding Tan, and their peers rose from modest roots to sustain the founding court—serving loyally inside and out while keeping honor intact.

sentences.zh: 而愉高謝百萬之貲，辭榮數畝之宅，弘止足之分，有廉讓之風者矣。

translations.literal: Yet Yu high declining million strings' wealth—declining glory several mu mansion—expanding stop-foot's portion—having modest yielding wind indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yu spurned riches and mansions—true exemplar of knowing when enough sufficed.

sentences.zh: 陶回陳邪佞之宜遠，明鬻賣之非宜，並補闕弼違，良可稱也。

translations.literal: Tao Hui displaying wicked flattery's ought-distance—clarifying selling-buying's not fitting—and repairing omissions aiding failures—truly praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hui exposed sycophants and barred slave markets—counsel as valuable as his grain relief.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：愉既公才，潭唯公望。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Yu already ducal talent—Tan only ducal renown.
translations.idiomatic: The verse praises Kong Yu's substance and Ding Tan's reputation.

sentences.zh: 領軍儒雅，平越忠亮。

translations.literal: Army leader refined Ru—Pacifying-Yue loyal bright.
translations.idiomatic: The general-education scholar led armies; the colonel who pacified the Yue stood loyal and bright.

sentences.zh: 君平料敵，彭祖弘益。

translations.literal: Junping gauged foes—Pengzu expanded benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Junping read battles; Pengzu enriched the state.

sentences.zh: 茂以象焚，群由匡厄。

translations.literal: Mao by elephant burned—Qun through Kuang hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao died like the ivory omen; Kong Qun survived Kuang Shu's spite.

sentences.zh: 陶回規過，言同金石。

translations.literal: Tao Hui corrected faults—words same metal stone.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hui's blunt counsel rang hard as bronze bells.
